notes.title: Beta 14.9 Test - Story Updates and Prologue
notes.content:
Today's build is on the test branch and includes a new prologue and a bunch of new stuff that will be used in the upcoming story content.
[list][*]When creating a new character you will start in the HammerHelm stronghold and play through a short prologue.
[*]The prologue and other quests have been updated to use the new quest dialogue system.
[*]The prologue also includes some quick backstory for what happened before we get to this point.
[*]The Wishing Well quest (Let's Get Ready to Grrrumble) appears much earlier now.
[*]Grrrumble's and Shaydee's quests now use the new quest dialogue system.
[*]Added the expanded quest dialogue to the end of the Lantern Quest to help give you some direction for what to do next.
[*]The Scarecrow and Orc quests have been updated to be a part of the new story. These updates were mostly quest dialogue related to add context and a couple of new quests added to them to tie them into the story.
[*]A few other updates that aren't live yet but will be used in the new story.[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/0e180f569e490e4648bee210096a2242653c1214.png[/img]

[b]Some info about how the main story quests will work. [/b]
In many RPGs you have a main story and then you have side quests. The main story quest is almost always active, meaning you have at least one quest related to the story the majority of your time in the game. 

HammerHelm is going to work different from this. I don't want there to be a main story related quest always active as that would detract from focusing on building the town. If I did that, there would always be this pressure to work on the story and not the town. I also don't want story quest content to force you to build specific buildings.

It's a balancing act between main questing and the town building and repeatable quests. So, the main story quest in HammerHelm takes place in parts that you start and finish and then there is a break for a while before the next part starts. If you've already played HammerHelm, this will work much in the same as the way the Scarecrow and Orc quests work. In fact, those two quests are now part 1 and part 2 of the main story and connect to each other as well as set the stage for the next part. Most of the updates to these quests are story/dialogue related so they play pretty much the same as before, but with more context added and some minor tweaks.

There will be smaller quests that act as bridges between the bigger main story quests too. Some of these "bridge quests" will focus on dialogue with a townsperson or other character, rather than quests to go do something or fight something. So they'll be really quick and include information that flows into the next main story quest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5a54fb5757854f7128eae145b85f6106c0c6a5c9.png[/img]

[b]Some important notes for playing the test build[/b]:
[list][*]You MUST make a new character to play this content. Do not load an existing save if you grab this build.
[*]The doors are turned off in the stronghold as I am writing optimization code related to them that isn't done yet.
[*]Don't walk to the end of the mine until you've completed the third quest and are directed to do so. This will be closed off and won't be accessible until after the third quest but since there are no doors you can access it.
[*]Once you start the prologue quest you must finish it. The quests are not set up to save and load midway through yet. It's four quests and is mostly dialogue, so it shouldn't take you more than a few minutes.
[*]When you finish the last prologue quest you are instantly teleported to the island. It's jarring, but there will a nicer fade added.[/list]
This build also includes a test version of a new quest loading system that will update your quests when loading a save in a different language than previously used. Right now the save system saves the actual text, so if you change the language and then load a save, it will remain in the old language. This new system uses the new language's translated text.

If you would like to check out the new content, you can get it by doing the following:

notes.title: In Development - The Deep Dwellers
notes.content:
Although they resemble what one might think a demon to look like, the Deep Dwellers are actually distantly related to Goblins and Orcs. Though they share some physical similarities, make no mistake, a Deep Dweller is a far more dangerous foe.

[i]Concept Art created by Ash Jackson[/i]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/d4dc1ab8ca4eb7bdce52d0955ccccb41fba76490.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/d4dc1ab8ca4eb7bdce52d0955ccccb41fba76490.png[/img][/url]
[i](click to see full size)[/i]

The Deep Dwellers wear strong armor capable of shrugging off attacks from weapons made from lesser materials, such as copper or iron. Many are known to wield magic to increase the effectiveness of their weapons in combat or cast powerful offensive spells.  

Nobody has seen a Deep Dweller for many centuries, but one must always be prepared when exploring the deeper areas of the world for once disturbed, their attacks are relentless. The only way to stop their advance is to destroy their leader. Doing this will break their resolve and send them back to the depths!

We're currently working on getting these guys in the game. Their models are done and we're tweaking some things with how they animate along with finishing the textures. I hope to have some animated versions to show you soon!

Also, after getting some feedback, I decided to expand the Trading system to include some more resources. I showed this on the [b]Discord[/b] channel a bit ago but wanted to put it here too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/ca9d8d3d2b33f5d84400c42fe52dc89bb60f9180.png[/img]

The idea is each resource has a trade value and a cost value. This way you can trade whatever you want and take whatever you want. I decided to go with the manufactured goods rather than raw resources. The value and cost of resources will change over time, probably twice an in-game day.

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
jon@hammerhelm.com
[list][*]My Twitter: https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios
[*]Discord Channel: discord.gg/soedesco[/list]

Today's update includes the new World Map feature!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/80e954f0a2229b47e06802e8e8a410801f4801b1.gif[/img]

The world map now shows the major static locations, such as your town, Shaydee's shop, Willow Grove, and more. Some of these update after you complete a quest, such as Shaydee's Shop initially just says "construction" when you mouse over it, but once you help Shaydee build his shop, the text updates. Similarly, Grrrumble's cave initially isn't on the map, but once you meet him, his location is permanently added.

Any quest locations outside of town and any quests where you need to speak with an NPC get a quest marker. Note not all quests have a quest marker. Most of the quests that require you to do something in town (such as the Broken Sewers quest or quests that ask you to use the Metalworker's furnace) don't have quest markers since they are in your town and the marker wouldn't be super helpful anyway. Also quests like the Cursed Trees don't have a quest marker since you can chop down any tree near the town. But quests with monster spawners, dungeons, caves/mines, and most others have quest markers added.

Your facing also updates to reflect which direction you are looking relative to the map.

This update also includes some fixes:
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused some extra buildings to appear on the map.
[*]Fixed a bunch of localization issues related to the Orc Quest.
[*]Fixed some controller input and mapping bugs.
[*]Fixed a bug that quest the second part of the "Big Distraction" quest to display text for the third part.[/list]
A more useful world map has been a big community request and I am super excited to have it live now. Thank you again everyone for the feedback and support!

notes.title: HammerHelm Development Update
notes.content:
[h1]HammerHelm Development Update[/h1]
It’s been a while since I wrote up a Development Update so I'd like to give you all a glimpse into what I am working on and what’s coming next!

A few things to keep in mind before we get started. All of this is work in progress. Some of this may change or not make it into the game at all depending on whether I’m happy with the results. And last, some of these are a bit of a ways off – especially the story.

Ok, let’s start!

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
Always first on my list is fixing any bugs. Boring I know, but top priority, so I’m listing it here. :)

[h1]Optimization - NPCs[/h1]
Part of this is already in the game but there is still more that I want to do. Thankfully I’m using a plug-in to help me optimize the NPCs so the process is pretty quick and I’m mostly at the point of tweaking numbers until I get a nice balance of visual quality vs. performance.

[h1]Optimization - Town Buildings[/h1]
Similar to the NPCs, this is already partly in the game as a few buildings have been optimized, but most haven’t been yet. Unlike the NPCs, this is a manual process and requires me to edit every building individually. I’m not an artist by any stretch of the imagination, so this is slow going, but so far, I like the results I am getting both visually and in performance. This is something I’ll be doing bit by bit as I work on other things.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/44e32106bb156f1f68c31571beb395201d189e87.jpg[/img]
[i](less tris is better performance!)[/i]

[h1]A Story[/h1]
This is the big feature I am working on and the one I am both the most excited and the most terrified to tell you about so early. :) It’s easily going to be the biggest thing I’ve ever added to the game. 

I’m still in the design phases for this and working out the details, but I have a lot of it fleshed out. Enough that work has already started on the assets to build a new location and some new monsters that will feature in the story.

Unlike the Scarecrow and Orc Quest and you will be able to travel back to your town during parts of the Story’s quests and this won’t be something you finish in one bite. Especially since the Scarecrow and Orc quests are going to be part of this story! You’ll also get to learn more about some of the characters you’ve already met on the island and meet some new ones too. Completing the story has some really cool rewards and will also unlock a new gameplay feature or two.

All of that said, I have some early work in progress shots I’d like to share. No spoilers, but I’m thinking some of you might be able to guess the new location. This is still quite a way from being complete but as I progress, I’ll continue to give you sneak peeks and sometime in the future I might put some things up on the test branch that you can check out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/36975666dbb3c62b6e0c070e1140ea3b221ab093.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/c641352562cf90477fcba5aadec8e57884b15b2d.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/fd99d3515be2145c93582e4c2b57dc98c6bffa18.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/da2faba2ece449747abc8339b6534908241963f3.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/a007c706bdd6035d8eb5289a572fb302e103ef71.jpg[/img]

[h1]Improved World Map[/h1]
The world map is being updated to be more dynamic. Things like the monster camps, quest locations, Grrrumble's cave, will be added as you get quests, rather than always being there. Work on this has already started and the artist who drew the current map is working on updating it so I can add and remove points of interest as you get quests and/or discover new things. I’ll likely be adding some more features to this such as mouse-over pop-ups and player facing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/07623da5e9504ca02a9b7c310a60e39aa67069c6.jpg[/img]

[h1]Updated Combat[/h1]
This one I’m not 100% sure on yet, but I want to make combat feel a bit better. As I’ve often said, I’m not trying to make a hardcore combat system. I want HammerHelm to feel mostly relaxing. But I think there are improvements and tweaks that I can make to help combat feel more fun without adding too many layers of complexity. In addition to refining the controls this might also include some active skills to replace some of the passive skills. Monsters might get some tweaks as well. I’m still designing how using skills would work, especially for controllers so again, grain of salt with this.

[h1]New Quests[/h1]
In addition to the big story quest I want to add more regular quests too, including the quests with the town item rewards. Most of this is coming up with ideas, both for the quest, and for the town items, but it’s been a while since I added new quests so I really want to work on some more.

[h1]New Music[/h1]
Still in the early phases so not much in the way of details yet. As this develops, I’ll be sharing more.

[h1]Better Tutorialization[/h1]
If “tutorialization” isn’t a word I’m officially making it one! What I mean by this is explaining things that aren’t necessarily obvious, such as how to place multiple mines or other features that are easy to miss. I don’t want to add more to the tutorial itself, but I think there are some things that could be explained better early on. If you have examples of things that you found complicated or a feature you didn’t even know existed at first, I’d love feedback on what you think could use better tutorialization.

[h1]Wrap Up[/h1]
I know that you’ve all probably noticed that I’ve been very focused on bug fixing, optimizations, and improvements to existing systems. Important stuff, but not terribly exciting. I felt it was important to let you all know that there are some other, really cool things going on in the background while I shore up the current game. Of everything here, aside from the bug fixing and optimizations, the updated World Map is probably the farthest along.

[h1]Thank you![/h1]
As always, thank you for all of your support, feedback, and ideas. I cannot say that or express how grateful I am for this community often enough. If you have ideas for new content or features that you’d like to see please feel free to share!


-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
jon@hammerhelm.com

•	My Twitter: https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios
•	Discord Channel: discord.gg/soedesco

notes.title: Beta 14.2 - Optimizations and Fixes
notes.content:
Another build today to add some optimizations and fix a few more reported issues.

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list][*]Optimized the Wooden House, Stone House, and Storehouse when first built. Basically this replaces the parts of the building that appear while it is being built with one combined object. This helps performance and I'll be rolling this out to other buildings over time.
[*]Optimized the NPCs. I turned the test for this off earlier today as it was causing the NPCs to glitch and get stuck. I'll likely be adding this to the monsters as well.
[*]Updated the rock optimization to fix an issue that made them change their color (darker gray) when you got closer to them.[/list]
[b]Updates based on feedback[/b]
[list][*]Lowered the time that tree parts remain in the world after a tree is chopped down from 3.5 seconds to 1.5 seconds. This should make it much easier to spot the collectable wood pieces.
[*]Made some combat refinements to remove the issue of clicking to attack right after you stop blocking to fail to start the attack.
[*]Refined the Herbalist UI to work better with a controller.[/list]

[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused the Telescope UI to display the wrong key to use to stop looking through it.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the close button in the Herbalist UI to not function with a controller.[/list]
Thank you again everyone for the feedback and support! I know I've been very focused on optimizations and fixes the past few weeks, but worry not - there is new content in the works too!

notes.title: Beta 13.0 - Resource Tools
notes.content:
Tonight's update includes the new resource tool system and some controller enhancements.

[b]Resource Tools[/b]
Pickaxes and hatchets have been added to the game! 

Two new equipment slots have been added to the "Equipped" part of the inventory UI, one for your pickaxe and the other for your hatchet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/d7e46c1ab916e696ec43696230ca98efbf983870.jpg[/img]

If you have a pickaxe or a hatchet in their slots, your character will automatically switch to use the correct tool based on what you are hitting. There is no need to manually switch using a hot key or opening your inventory. If you swing at nothing or attack a monster, your weapon will appear.

I made a quick video to show off how it works.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d3EUB4iZqmI&feature=youtu.be
There are four levels for each tool, copper, iron, jade, and diamond.

For trees the better the hatchet the less hits it takes to chop it down. The same is true for mining stone with a pickaxe. For ore, you need the right pick to mine ore deposits. Copper picks can mine copper and iron. Iron picks can mine copper through jade. Jade picks can mine copper through diamond. And diamond picks can mine any of the ore including Blood Stone.

You'll also need a hatchet to smash Alchemy Logs, Supply Crates, and Dungeon Crates. These all still take only one hit regardless of what kind of hatchet you have.

Copper, iron, and jade tools can be crafted by the Metalworker. These can also be crafted at the Weaponsmith, in addition to the diamond tools. Metalworkers can also craft jade ingots. This is to make sure you can make jade tools if you haven't placed a Weaponsmith or Armorsmith yet. If you start a new character you get a copper pickaxe along with your weapons and potions.

This update also changes out the starting axe with a starting hammer. You can see that in the above video as well.

[b]Controller Updates[/b]
[list][*]Mappable buttons. This is still in testing so if you encounter any issues with it please let me know. 
[*]You can now use a controller to place and rotate furniture.
[*]You can now invert the right stick on a controller.
[*]You can change the sensitivity of the left and right sticks on a controller.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the footstep volume slider to ignore controller input.[/list]

I have to admit this was one of the more fun updates I've worked on in a long time. I really enjoyed getting the pickaxes and hatchets to automatically appear before your "attack" hit the object. It feels really good and I want to say thank you to everyone who suggested adding pickaxes and hatchets.

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

[list][*]My Twitter: https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios

notes.title: In Development - Pickaxes and Axes
notes.content:
"Chopping down a tree with a hammer is weird." "Breaking a rock with a sword makes no sense." 

I hear you! Like the shared resource between inventory and storehouse, this is another one of those things I've been stubborn about for a while, but I can't argue - the current implementation *does* look weird. 

The main reason HammerHelm lets you get resources using your weapon is I didn't want to force players to have to manually switch between their weapon, their pickaxe, an axe, etc. Even making it a hotkey still feels cumbersome to me.

So, I'm developing a system to automatically switch to the correct weapon/item and have an artist creating axes and pickaxes for you to craft!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/d832a4a0c805244ba80c523d2abd00724ba2a067.jpg[/img]

The concepts were created by the same artist who made the apiaries, beehives, and trellis and she's also working on the in-game models.

The hammer in the above image is going to be the new starting weapon. I think a HammerHelm Dwarf should start out with a hammer! :)

There are four kinds of pickaxes and axes. Tress can be felled with any of the axes with better axes requiring less hits to knock the tree down. The same is true for the pickaxes and getting quality stone. For ore deposits, you will need the right pickaxe to get the ore.

Copper pickaxes can mine Copper and Iron.
Iron pickaxes can mine Jade
Jade pickaxes can mine Gold and Diamond.
And the Diamond pickaxe can mine Blood Stone.

Pickaxes can also mine anything at lower ore levels, so a Jade pickaxe can also mine Copper, Iron, and Jade. I'm, still debating whether a weaker pickaxe *can't* get ore or if it requires double the number of hits. Either way, making an axe or pickaxe won't be a big investment and you should easily have one by the time you get to the next ore level. These items will also NOT have durability so once you have one, you're good to go. 

My goal with this system isn't to make getting resources more difficult but rather to make the process of chopping a tree or mining ore feel and look better. So the actual cost in resources to make these will likely be pretty low. 

The tutorial will be updated to get you your first Copper Pickaxe and Copper Axe before the part where you make your first weapon. Existing saves will be able to just craft the items depending on what ore you have available. 

Right now I'm thinking these will be craftable at the Metalworker. I'll add the higher ore ingots to the Metalworker as well, although they'll cost a bit more than the Armorsmith's or Weaponsmith's ingots. I don't want to put the pickaxes and axes exclusively on those two jobs though, just in case someone gets to Jade Ore before placing those buildings. I don't want them to gate advancement in this system.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/b8ea76e8e93e6c5283ccdbc4bc06f31f9f7d118d.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/b8ea76e8e93e6c5283ccdbc4bc06f31f9f7d118d.jpg[/img][/url]
[i](click to see full size)[/i]

The Equip Panel of the Inventory UI will be updated to include two new slots. One for your axe and the other for your pickaxe. Once equipped the system will automatically choose the correct item depending on what you are hitting.

Testing the system using the Jade Hammer and Jade Axe as stand-ins. Your weapons is the default in case you swing at nothing or break a create, alchemy log, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/73445b8eaa518a3e3c2274dea7833838448a1355.gif[/img]

This gif isn't the best quality (we're limited to 3mbs for uploads in announcements) so I also put up a video on my YouTube account so you can see it in action.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1VIL-tXeRk4&feature=youtu.be

Once again, I want to say thank you to everyone for your support and feedback. I hope you all enjoy this once we finish it!

notes.title: Beta 12.1 - More Mines
notes.content:
Today's update includes the new mines system, an improvement to the townspeople UI controller support, and some fixes and tweaks.

[b]New Mines[/b]
The new mine system allows you to place additional mines to get more miners and get access to better ore rather than from placing the Stonemason and then having to wait for the quests to unlock the next ore. Existing saves will automatically be converted to use the new system so you don't have to start over to use it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/8ea6ee2dd06213491e45e4db32903ffe420395b4.jpg[/img]

[b]New Saves[/b]
If you start a new game the tutorial related to the mine will be slightly different. Mainly, there is no existing mine on the map when you start out! So rather than asking a townsperson to clear the mine, the quest will allow you to place a mine. 

[b]Existing Saves[/b]
If you have a save that includes at least one assigned miner your save will automatically be updated to use the new multi-mine system. For example, if you have 3 miners, when you load your save with this build, the game will automatically place three mines and assign each of your miners to one of those mines. After that, you'll be able to place new mines to get more miners.

[b]Placing Mines[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/3a8350e729747e3ad921bae622f71031e79806ff.jpg[/img]

The build system has been updated to add two areas to place mines. These are located at the top of the screen in the shot above. In that shot, I'm actually placing a fourth mine on the left side. The three mines on the right were auto-placed by the system because my save had three miners.

The tutorial mine requires one copper ore (along with wood and stone) to place. One of the things I have to add is a safety check to give you one copper if you use all of it crafting ingots.

After that, each subsequent mine requires one ore of the next type. So the next mine requires an iron ore and the one after that will require unrefined jade, and so on. As soon as you place a new mine you'll get a quest to clear out the mine. This new quest will appear even if you are at the open quest cap. After completing this quest you'll gain the ability to assign a new miner and you'll unlock the ore that the mine was built with. The ore unlock applies to all miners. 

So, after the tutorial mine, if you place the next mine with iron ore, you'll get a second miner and you can assign iron ore to both of the miners if you want to.

You cannot place a mine will the quest to clear out the previous mine is active. Also, for existing saves, if you've already unlocked diamond and/or blood stone, you won't be reset back to gold ore because you only have four mines. You will however be able to place a fifth and sixth mine assuming you have the requisite diamond ore and/or blood stone ore to do so.

Here I just placed that fourth mine and have the quest to clear it out.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5ed3a6a5a7bbb7dc32a78a6fe5059a9d6c3c05ef.jpg[/img]

Note one big change is mines no longer have ore in them for the player to obtain. Quests involving caves and other mines will continue to work as usual. I did this for a few of reasons, mostly related to balance. Overall this system should allow you to get ore faster since unlocking new mines and assigning miners is way more predictable than it was in the current system where you had to wait for quests to get the next ore type. Plus you can now have up to six miners!

[b]Townspeople UI[/b]
The townspeople UI has been updated to improve controller support. In the previous version, you had to use horizontal d-pad movements to use the toggles and press Y to activate them, while navigating the list of townspeople used vertical d-pad inputs and the A button. This was confusing. This update now uses all d-pad inputs to move around the UI and only the A button is needed to activate a toggle or press a button. Scrolling and navigation has also been improved.

This build also includes some fixes and balance updates:
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused Fisherman and Hunters to get stuck at home after a Storehouse was infested.
[*]You can now open the options menu when underground.
[*]You cannot save the game while underground. The save buttons have also been updated to make it clear they are deactivated.
[*]Increased the amount of storage in the Storehouses for a variety of resources including most of the alchemy resources and handles.[/list]
I have some other small things that I want to get in the next build. These are almost done, but I didn't want to delay this update:
[list][*]16:10 screen ratio support.
[*]Optimization updates for caves, dungeons, and the haunted mansion.
[*]Updated and much better looking Steam Achievement Icons (these are in progress and already look way better!)
[*]Improved up and down camera rotation.[/list]

Thank you everyone for your support and feedback!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: Beta 12 Test - New Mines
notes.content:
Today's update is a test build for the new mine system I mentioned in the previous announcement. This new system allows you to place additional mines to get more miners and get access to better ore rather than from placing the Stonemason and then having to wait for the quests to unlock the next ore. This is a really big change and it's backwards compatible with existing saves so I thought it best to upload it as a test build. I'm still working on some additions to the system, such as moving the mines, but the main parts are done.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/8ea6ee2dd06213491e45e4db32903ffe420395b4.jpg[/img]

[b]New Saves[/b]
If you start a new game the tutorial related to the mine will be slightly different. Mainly, there is no existing mine on the map when you start out! So rather than asking a townsperson to clear the mine, the quest will allow you to place a mine. 

[b]Existing Saves[/b]
If you have a save that includes at least one assigned miner your save will automatically be updated to use the new multi-mine system. For example, if you have 3 miners, when you load your save with this build, the game will automatically place three mines and assign each of your miners to one of those mines. After that, you'll be able to place new mines to get more miners. Getting this to work with existing saves actually took more time than building the system itself, but was fun to figure out and implement!

[b]Placing Mines[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/3a8350e729747e3ad921bae622f71031e79806ff.jpg[/img]

The build system has been updated to add two areas to place mines. These are located at the top of the screen in the shot above. In that shot, I'm actually placing a fourth mine on the left side. The three mines on the right were auto-placed by the system because my save had three miners.

The tutorial mine requires one copper ore (along with wood and stone) to place. One of the things I have to add is a safety check to give you one copper if you use all of it crafting ingots.

After that, each subsequent mine requires one ore of the next type. So the next mine requires an iron ore and the one after that will require unrefined jade, and so on. As soon as you place a new mine you'll get a quest to clear out the mine. This new quest will appear even if you are at the open quest cap. After completing this quest you'll gain the ability to assign a new miner and you'll unlock the ore that the mine was built with. The ore unlock applies to all miners. 

So, after the tutorial mine, if you place the next mine with iron ore, you'll get a second miner and you can assign iron ore to both of the miners if you want to.

You cannot place a mine will the quest to clear out the previous mine is active. Also, for existing saves, if you've already unlocked diamond and/or blood stone, you won't be reset back to gold ore because you only have four mines. You will however be able to place a fifth and sixth mine assuming you have the requisite diamond ore and/or blood stone ore to do so.

Here I just placed that fourth mine and have the quest to clear it out.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5ed3a6a5a7bbb7dc32a78a6fe5059a9d6c3c05ef.jpg[/img]

Note one big change is mines no longer have ore in them for the player to obtain. Quests involving caves and other mines will continue to work as usual. I did this for a few of reasons, mostly related to balance. Overall this system should allow you to get ore faster since unlocking new mines and assigning miners is way more predictable than it was in the current system where you had to wait for quests to get the next ore type. Plus you can now have up to six miners! I still want to the tutorial mine to have ore inside though so you have a bit of a headstart creating copper items early on.

I also have some other things I might add to this to make getting a new mine more interesting, but don't want to talk about them just yet in case I decide they aren't a good fit. I'd like the quest to unlock the mine to involve more than just killing monsters but we'll see how that goes.

If you want to try out the new system and help test it, you can get this build by following these instructions:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - NewMineTest1 - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game and you should see "Beta 12 - test" in the title screen.

[b]VERY IMPORTANT - if you load an existing save or make a new save and get the new mines, those saves will NOT be compatible with the current live build. So I recommend making a backup of your save or just sticking with the test build until I create the live one.[/b]

To get back to the main build:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the main client

Thank you again everyone for your feedback and suggestions. I really hope you enjoy this new system!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: Beta 11.6.1 - Quick Fixes and What's Next
notes.content:
Today's build is a quick one that includes fixes for missing textures for the Stone House (when upgraded from a Wooden House) and the stairs inside the Orc Shaman Hut.

The last couple of updates have been a bit small because I'm working on a big change to the way mines work. 

The new system will allow you to place a mine, rather than have a townsperson unblock it for you. And to get more miners, you'll be able to place more mines, rather than getting them after placing a Stonemason! Each mine will require an ore to create and the ore type increases with each mine you place. So the first mine you place requires a Copper Ore to place a second one you'll need an Iron Ore. And so on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/8ea6ee2dd06213491e45e4db32903ffe420395b4.jpg[/img]

You'll be able to have up to five mines and I'm doing some testing to determine whether the tutorial mine will require an ore or not. Basically I want to make sure you can get additional miners at a good rate so likely the tutorial mine will not require copper and the second mine will. This means to get a fifth mine you'll need a gold ore rather than a diamond ore.

This is actually a huge change to the way HammerHelm manages mining, quests related to the mine, and miners themselves. In addition to updating the tutorial and how assigning miners works, I also want to make sure this change is compatible with existing saves. New mines will also allow any ore to be mined from it. So for example, once you place the mine that required an Iron Ore, the other mines will also be able to produce Iron Ore too. If I make the fifth mine require a gold ore, then you'll unlock the last two ore  types (Diamond and Blood Stone) through the current quest.

I'm hoping to have this update ready this weekend. I think it's a way more fun way of getting more miners and add some more structures to your town.

notes.title: Beta 11.3 - By Popular Request
notes.content:
This update is a long time coming and I'll admit, I've pushed against doing this for a long time, despite the fact that it has come up more than a few times. 

Today's build combines the storehouse resources and the resources in your backpack when checking to see if you can build a structure or craft an item. So no more having to go back to the storehouse to get that one piece of leather or dropping off wood to place a new building! The system removes items from your backpack first and then from the storehouse if more are needed.

Note the town UI will continue to only display the amount of resources in the storehouse and the inventory UI only displays what's in your backpack. Dwarves who use resources to make things for the town, such as the Carpenter, will continue to only use resources from the Storehouse. However, the crafting and building UI will update based on the combined amounts when determining whether to show the amount needed in red or green.

This update also adds the new resources to the resource tracking UI.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/c6f2bc4b7f8666ba59722825b46558beb3573b7c.jpg[/img]

After playing with the system for a while I have to say...you all were right. This is so much better! Humble pie actually tastes pretty good when it leads to something more fun. :)

So, thank you again everyone for your feedback and support!

notes.title: Beta 11.2 - Townspeople Traits and Combat Improvements
notes.content:
Today's build includes two pretty big changes to the townspeople traits system and to combat, specifically monster AI.

[b]Townspeople Traits[/b]
New Dwarves will now have a significantly reduced chance to have two negative traits. They will usually have either one positive and one negative or two positive traits.

[b]Combat[/b]
Monster AI has been updated to make their attacks a bit more frequent. Monsters will now sometimes immediately attack as soon as they get in melee range. in the previous system monsters would be reset if you left melee range, creating situations where monsters would never attack. Monsters have also had their wind-up timer reduced so there will be slightly less warning before they attack, but still time to block or dodge. Monsters have also had their special attack probably increased slightly. Overall these changes should make combat more engaging while still remaining easy to understand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/b20a4b5307388b77b03a8617ec262a185a9acdfd.jpg[/img]

Monster mages have also received some improvements. Goblin mages will now continue to turn face you during most of their casting "wind up" phase. Prior to this change, the goblin mage attack was usually wildly off target if you moved around. You'll still have time to dodge or move away from their attack, but you'll need to time it a bit now!

This build also fixes a bug that sometimes caused the Goblin Mage lightning attack to register a hit when you were close to it, but not in it.

I'll likely continue to do some minor tweaking to combat. My goal is to keep combat light and not super difficult, but I also want it to be more engaging and fun!

notes.title: Beta 11 - Roof Colors and Monster Attacks
notes.content:
Today's build includes a big update to the roof coloring system, a new dungeon entrance, and an improved monster special attack system!

[b]Roof Colors[/b]
Ever since I added the ability to change the roof color of houses, I've been asked to make it available for all buildings. So I did! With the new roof coloring system, any building's roof can be colored. The system allows you to set each building's roof color individually as well as setting all house roofs the same and all other buildings the same.

All houses yellow and all other buildings blue.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/4a2fdb6c588ceab590faea6c489020f62a17d6c2.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5fc129849e6d09e51664086fcba4c9a902c9232a.jpg[/img]

There are 17 colors to choose from. If you think I missed a color that you'd like to have please let me know. It's fairly easy to add more. :)

[b]Monster Special Attacks[/b]
I updated the monster special attacks system to make the special attacks more frequent. In the old system they almost never happened. The attacks are mostly the same with a few minor tweaks. Combat should be a bit more interesting now!

The Orc smash attack cannot be blocked. You can tell an Orc has this ability if you see one wielding a big stone hammer.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/08a3c134cf025123dbb4249613becd49ea7b6300.gif[/img]

The Skeleton trip attack is sneaky and also cannot be blocked. Skeletons who can perform this attack wield halberds.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/6c34f03bdfa68f40d742fb199b6fab8b4af47dab.gif[/img]

The Goblin stabbity-stab-stab attack can be blocked, however you must remain in the block stance for each attack! Goblins who can perform this attack wield curved swords.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/60e48bf8db6ca4027721013aff0f874452275083.gif[/img]

Ratman with twin daggers can perform double-strike attack. And Mushroomen with twin clubs can perform a spinning attack.

Updated dungeon entrance!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/c94a9f27d3e47eb7596e2381c08e544f8d9a31ce.jpg[/img]

This was literally the oldest object still in HammerHelm so it was way overdue for a refresh! You may not be able to see it in the screenshot, but the skull's eyes have little flames in them.

notes.title: Beta 10.3 - Memory Optimization and Combat
notes.content:
Today's build includes some more improvements to the combat flow, new shop signs, and a big memory optimization.

I've refined the animation controller and combat system some more to make transitioning from rolling and blocking into power attacks much better. In the old system if your character finished a roll and you immediately pressed the power attack button, sometimes nothing would happen. This delay was actually being caused by the way the animation controller was set up for the character. The new system is way better and allows you to start a power attack immediately.

In the gif below you can see there is no delay now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/ffd4aa0f35c3b4f8f674bc346956f1c958202837.gif[/img]


New shopkeeper signs! Every shop has a new, much improved, symbol. And, some buildings that were missing signs now have them, including the Fishing Pier, the Infirmary, and the Mage Tower!

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/4a73f5a08f8cd10bcb55e3310fcd1a2afe8af38b.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/4a73f5a08f8cd10bcb55e3310fcd1a2afe8af38b.jpg[/img][/url]
[i](click to see full size)[/i]


If you look at Metalworker Shop on the left of the image you will also see the new ingots.

This build also includes a big memory optimization that reduced HammerHelm's memory use by about 15%! Most of this was related to optimizing the town so that all buildings now share the same texture. This change also bumped up framerate a little bit. One thing you may notice is some of the building roof colors are a bit different. This was a huge update and affected a ton of objects in the world in addition to the buildings. This was all done manually as well so it's possible I missed an object or two. So, if you see any bright pink/purple objects in the world, that's the result of a missing texture. Please let me know what object it was and where it was and I'll update it.

I want to do some experimenting first, but this change might also allow me to make all building roofs colorable! More on that later.

This build also includes some other improvements and fixes.

[*]Fixed a bug related to the Lantern Quest.[/list]

notes.title: Beta 10.2 - Feedback Fixes and Balance
notes.content:
Today's update includes some balance changes and bug fixes based on player feedback!

[b]Combat Improvements[/b]

I adjusted the animation controller for the player to make combat more smooth. You should notice that you can transition between attacking, rolling, and power attacks much more quickly now. Still working on improving this as I dive deeper into setting up animation controllers. 

These changes should fix the bugs where you use a power attack or kick and the attack doesn't occur (but your cooldown does get reset) and the bug where rolling would sometimes not move you.

[b]A Bunch of Other Good Stuff[/b]

[list][*]Reduced the amount of monster parts needed to craft a monster head trophy by about 30% - 50%.
[*]Doubled the chance of a monster part spawning as loot.
[*]Reduced the amount of resources needed to make the new decor items including the Firefly Lamppost, Apiaries, and the Trellis.
[*]Reduced the Quality Wood required to build a The Metalworker Shop from 25 to 15. I made this change because sometimes if you run through the tutorial quickly there isn't enough wood collected yet to build the shop and I didn't want there to be a delay.
[*]The Missing Saw will now correctly be removed from your inventory at the end of the Gazebo Quest. If you finished this quest and still have the saw, it will be removed when you load your save with this update.
[*]You can now open the treasure chest from the Shroomin' quest without having to close the NPC Dialogue UI.
[*]Made the Gold Axe a bit ticker as it looked too flat.
[*]If you place a farm in an area that has a road the plot will now correctly turn fully into dirt rather than leave behind the road. A bit difficult to grow crops in cobblestone!
[*]If you save your game with auto-sprint enabled, your character will remain in auto-sprint when loading the save. No need to toggle it on every time you load.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the dynamic occlusion system to fail to start until you opened the build menu. If you noticed a dip in performance the past few days, this fix should resolve it.
[*]Increased the delay between casting when a mage or the Lich uses their close range AOE attack.[/list]

Thank you again to everyone who sends me feedback. Your bug reports, comments, and ideas always give me a new perspective on the game, one I cannot get on my own, and I really appreciate it!

notes.title: Beta 10 - New Resources, Decor, and more!
notes.content:
Today's build includes the new Resource Gathering and Decor feature and a bunch of other cool stuff!

[b]Wilderness Resources[/b]

The world of HammerHelm just got a lot more interesting! 

While traveling between your quests and your town you can find valuable resources that help keep your townspeople happy, give you more resources to craft items, and allow you to place new structures in your town and your home!

Scattered around the map you can find a bunch of different resources, including:

[b]Beehives[/b] - used to make Apiaries. When looking for these keep an ear out for the tell tale buzzing!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5aa4a973b8854789c680027dfd8cb849bb0a36c4.gif[/img]


[b]Rose Bushes and Fireflies[/b] - allow you to place Rose Bushes, Rose Trellises, and Firefly Lamps for your town and your home.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/12292f780254c070a41a7906b96bb44fac3625bd.gif[/img]


[b]Cherry Blossom and Birch Tree Seeds[/b] - allow you to place Birch Trees and Cherry Blossoms
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/8850a2dc1958160914c5456e5a2017b808bf0705.gif[/img]


[b]Medium Ore Deposits and Small Ore Deposits[/b] - contain a small amount of ore
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5625fa766c4ba7cd694e7c8fd2697a94cca91eb0.gif[/img]


[b]Supply Crates [/b]- can contain leather, raw meat, raw veggies, wheat, cotton, handles, or coal.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/823e51b5114ec9f5f1c19368f408c096ba4c2d33.gif[/img]


[b]Alchemy Logs[/b] - can contain any of the alchemy ingredients. Similar to ore deposits, what you find depends on how far you have progressed.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/8416ea5ca089f7e2ce55f3b175b0e55c96faa0bb.gif[/img]


The system starts out placing only a few of each but as time progresses in the game, you'll find these items become slightly more available. I’ll likely play around with how often they spawn and how many spawn over time. But they aren't meant to be too common.

Some resources are found more often in specific areas of the map, so pay attention to where you find them so you can go back later and look for more!

[b]New Town and Home Décor[/b]

This update includes seven new décor items for your town and your home, including:

[b]Apiaries[/b] - Placing an Apiary near your Breweries will improve the mood buff bonus from having Beer. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/6f96fde17271cbb0251ce65e0345f6a8d36e8429.jpg[/img]


[b]Rose Bushes and a Rose Trellis[/b]

[b]Birch Trees And Cherry Blossoms[/b]

[b]Firefly Lamppost[/b]

Rose Bushes, Trellises, Birch Trees, Firefly Lampposts and Cherry Blossoms all improve Town Beauty.

[b]Firefly Wall Lamp and Firefly Standing Lamp[/b] (player house)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/93669c9ab9970ee5ee6d9a770751fba10f284585.gif[/img]


But this is just the start. This update includes a LOT more!

[b]New Level Up Effect with Spinning Hammers[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/cda4dac87f66aca34af74927744a23ec4a716382.gif[/img]


[b]A new quest to get a lantern for your character[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/ab5ca67ac509f52700348154b380cd6e4fdc9271.jpg[/img]


[b]Updated grass texture and flowers[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/2427357bdf229198474628094f0d0297ec5ced8d.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/f7004cb7bc7e7f46d98da6835336ef968de2e09b.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/206f0539f2cba6d7f65a7b8692b011a5d8f7b7e9.gif[/img]


All of the UI have been updated to allow you track your town's resources and give what you find to the town!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/379432c2940716fa5163c120a2258b2be8872a1d.jpg[/img]


And there’s even more!

[b]Town Updates[/b]
[list][*]Increased the build area for the town by about 10%.
[*]Picking up a Brewery now correctly removes the entire path
[*]Fixed a big that sometimes caused placing a Gazebo to fail to load the Gazebo asset
[*]Fixed a couple of bugs related to the Town Resource manager UI
[*]Fixed the blocking volumes on the Brewery so NPCs won't walk through the walls
[*]Fixed some bugs related to mood affecting structures such as sewers, water wells, etc.[/list]

[b]Economy Updates[/b]
[list][*]Having a Woodchopper allows you to chop a tree in three hits rather than four
[*]Increased the amount of ore needed for armor and weapons a small amount to account for finding more ore in the wilderness
[*]Updated a bunch of the resource icons to look better and changed the beer icon from a mug to a keg[/list]

[b]Combat Improvements[/b]
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused Dash Attack to not do any damage
[*]The potion cooldown graphic will no longer appear when closing the Build menu
[*]Added text making it more clear that pressing ESC cancels your target
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Kick tutorial UI to display the wrong key
[*]Monsters will no longer slide towards you when knocked down and will remain in place until they get back up
[*]Randomly spawned monster camps (those that aren't tied to a quest) will now have campfires, making them a bit easier to spot
[/list]

[b]Controller Updates[/b]
[list][*]Added full 360 directional movement when using the left stick
[*]The left stick can now be used to interact with the UI in addition to the D-Pad
[*]Jumping with a controller now has height
[*]Added the close button to the Settings menu for controllers[/list]

[b]Other Changes and Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused the UI for buttons to read ESCAPE rather than ESC
[*]Fixed a bug related to the display of shadows
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the player to not perform a run animation when strafing
[*]Fixed a bug that caused you to get stuck on the second Orc Hut quest
[*]Updated sandstone so you always automatically collect it after breaking it apart
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Dwarves to not get a mood buff from Beer (worst bug ever!)
[*]Fixed a bug related to the place furniture UI
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Hunters to get confused when getting a quest
[*]You will no longer get the Orc Beachhead quest twice at the same time
[*]Fixed a few typos[/list]

I want to give a big shout out to [b]Alexis Bierschbach[/b] – she created the art for the Beehives, Apiaries, Rose Trellis, the new terrain flowers, and the Firefly Lamp. You can check out some of her work here:  https://www.artstation.com/fraiselin. She’s also working on some other stuff for HammerHelm, but that’s for another time. ;)

This update has been one of the most fun updates I’ve worked on since launching HammerHelm. I want to thank everyone who gave me feedback and suggestions as the new features were in development and testing. 

I appreciate all of the feedback and support!

[list][*]Rose Bushes

notes.title: In Development Update
notes.content:
The resource spawning system has grown once again to include a new resource type - supply crates! 

Supply crates can be smashed just like the crates in dungeons, except these crates can yield many different resources, including:
[list][*]Leather
[*]Raw veggies
[*]Raw Meat
[*]Cotton
[*]Wheat
[*]Handles
[*]Coal[/list]
It's a small amount from each crate, but it gives you a chance to collect resources that your town may be short on or get resources that your town can't currently produce at all yet. I might also add a small, short duration, mood buff for the town when you drop off these resources.

Smashing a supply crate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/823e51b5114ec9f5f1c19368f408c096ba4c2d33.gif[/img]

And I added butterflies to the Rose Trellis. I never knew how much I needed butterflies in my town until I did this! :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/45494aaeb7b69f672c66e0920019a1a217356dc7.gif[/img]

You'll also be able to place a group of Rose Bushes, in addition to the Rose Trellis, using the Roses you find in the world.

An updated shot of all of the new stuff, including the Rose Bush. When you place them in town they'll come in groups of three or four.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/3ea39a0119353020fa4dd9c8f6255524faf9042e.jpg[/img]

I'm also working on some other things, not specifically related to the resource system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/206f0539f2cba6d7f65a7b8692b011a5d8f7b7e9.gif[/img]

A much better effect for smashing the gold crates in dungeons. Also note the little lantern on the Dwarf's hip. That will be craftable using Iron Ore and Fireflies. It will automatically turn on at night and when underground. I might add other uses for the new resources as well - either new things for your character or new things for your home, or both!

With the addition of the new resources and the supply crates I'm going to update the Town Resource UI to show the new resources and the Storehouse UI to allow you to add and remove the resources found in Supply Crates.

Another thing I am working on is improving the look of the world a bit, starting with the ground texture and the grass. In this shot you can see the current (left) vs. my latest test (right). I think the right looks way better as the current ground and grass don't match particularly well and the ground has too much dark contrast. The grass on the right also has some slight color variance in it in addition to matching the ground a bit better.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/010cb2a55098401cd0bebf733c28f0c0be51f2da.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/010cb2a55098401cd0bebf733c28f0c0be51f2da.jpg[/img][/url]
[i](click to see larger version}[/i]

I also have a few other things in the works too. This is going to be a pretty big update! I was hoping to launch it on Sunday, but I think I'm going to need some more time. Adding all of these resources also means I need to balance out some of the numbers and with the new decor, I want to make the buildable area larger. Changing that area actually affects a lot of other things, but it's worth doing. I'd hate to add all of this stuff and then have you all run out of space to place them!

As always, feedback is encouraged and welcomed! Thank you all for your continued support of HammerHelm. Making this game has been a real dream come true and I am so glad to have all of you with me on this journey!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: Beta 9.7 - UI Updates and Collectibles Progress
notes.content:
Beta 9.7 includes some more updates to the UI to better support controller inputs and localized text in addition to some other changes and fixes.
[list][*]Added the tutorial guides for building and the townspeople UI to use controller instructions when using a controller.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused jumping when using a controller to fail to actually jump. The animation played, but the character didn't jump up.
[*]Updated more text to support keyboard vs. controller localized text.
[*]Fixed a bug with the close button in the intro story UI.[/list]
Also, a quick look at the current in-game assets for the collectibles system. After getting some great feedback, I decided to add both ore and alchemy ingredients to the world resource spawner that also handles the new stuff like the beehives and bags of seeds.

A screenshot of all of them together. Note, we're still working on the Trellis, specifically the leaves and flowers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/303720acfca4e8846f3a58e853c6d063727f11ba.jpg[/img]

The smaller ore deposits will appear in the world as part of the resource spawner. The large deposit will continue to appear in caves and in quests. The medium size deposit will yield between 4 and 5 ore and the smallest will give 1 to 2. The large ore will continue to give 10 to 11 ore. The logs with the alchemy resources will likely give around 5 of that resource.

A Beehive with bees
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/5aa4a973b8854789c680027dfd8cb849bb0a36c4.gif[/img]

A Firefly Lamppost
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/7ec2f24b291978da1611d2f9676d31b456a9d69a.gif[/img]

As part of the collectible resources update I'm also going to be balancing the game a bit. Mostly on the weapons, armor, and potions. Since you'll be getting more resources from exploring, rather than only from quests, I'm going to need to adjust the resource requirements for the items. The net effect of crafting items should be similar to the current rate, perhaps a touch longer. I don't want it to feel like a grind though so once the update goes live I'll definitely be looking for your feedback!

Another balance change I am considering is making chopping down trees take three hits rather than four once you have a Woodchopper and also increasing the amount of spawned resources in the new system once you have a Woodchopper as well. I think that building needs a buff!

Happy Mother's Day to all of the moms out there! Hope everyone continues to stay safe and healthy and as always, thank you so much for the feedback and support!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: In Development - Collectibles and New Town Decor
notes.content:
I'm working on a new system to add some variety and some reward for exploring the map. One of the pieces of feedback that I get is the journey from town to a quest and then back again can get a bit boring as there is little to discover or see between destinations. The Collectible Decor system will add some things to the world that you can find and use to improve your town!

To start, there will be five resources to discover on the island - Beehives, Cherry Blossom Seeds, Birch Tree Seeds, Roses, and Fireflies. 

Collecting enough of these will allow you to build special structures for your town, including Apiaries, Cherry Blossom Trees, Birch Trees, A Rose Trellis, and a special Firefly Lamppost.

Some Concept Art

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/33e70b10e67d889bef5327dd83425c52d1a4b0a8.jpg[/img]

I made a quick mock-up of how the beehives will appear using the concept. They'll be found on the small birch trees. Beehives are more commonly found to the east of the town.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/2de6d9311254d12cb9e750ae449893a554125979.jpg[/img]

A bag of seeds hidden in a bush. Seeds for Birch Trees and Cherry Blossoms are often found north of the town, with Cherry Blossom seeds being more prevalent near the ruins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/4a67f073edcbbe11ee3f050e2144495fc4b23536.jpg[/img]

A Cherry Blossom placed in a town!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/1643c2bcaa3ab2c7d3cb4ad3671d0e00b0b4ad3c.jpg[/img]

Fireflies. These are more common near Willow Grove.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/d06a5a4669543e4cf91cd7c6f6f39225a06510c1.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Beta 9.5 - Controller and Dynamic Text Improvements
notes.content:
Beta 9.5 is a big update to the controller and how dynamic text is created in HammerHelm. 

This update includes a new controller layout.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/26b8a6142218aceac96acc405f3db0bb9b7def69.jpg[/img]

The biggest change is a the d-pad radial menu. This appears when you press the Y button if you don't have anything to interact with such as a treasure chest or an NPC to speak with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/e134f7b10b3e8a0bbd69de9d5a5e6ed4a3e49223.jpg[/img]

Pressing the d-pad in the direction of the button opens that UI. This frees up the other buttons to be used for specific things, rather than doubling up on having a button do something combat related in one instance and something UI related in another. Since they are freed up now, pressing the Right Stick will cycle quests and the X button now cycles monster targets. You can also press down on the d-pad when a potion is selected to place it back into your inventory.

In addition, all of the UI that asks you to press a button or press a key has been updated to use icons rather than embedding the key in the text. This will make translated HammerHelm a lot easier. 

You can see this in the Speak with NPC text along with the cycle quest and build/town text. If you change the key in the options menu, the keys in the UI will update with the new key. They system will also switch to showing controller buttons if you use a controller.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/fc99ddeaddeba252329e77b65df354913861168b.jpg[/img]

I've added a new keybind specific to cycling quests. It defaults to the B key.

This build also includes a fix to resolve a bug that caused the skill point bar to not update properly when loading a save.

Sorry I haven't had an update for a bit as I've been sick the past week. Feeling better now and really happy to be able to get this update out to all of you!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: WIP - New User Interface
notes.content:
In addition to working on new content, fixes, and optimizations, we've also been working on a new UI! 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/6829227d2a74ee2a03d91b7a7258bdce031027fd.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/6829227d2a74ee2a03d91b7a7258bdce031027fd.jpg[/img][/url]
[i]click to see full size[/i]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/82eedd0c8399625cee22167690c70466c15fae5f.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/82eedd0c8399625cee22167690c70466c15fae5f.jpg[/img][/url]
[i]click to see full size[/i]

I've been very lucky to work with a designer at Soedesco on cleaning up and improving HammerHelm's UI. It's awesome to have support like that!

The new look is much cleaner than the current look. The icons are nicer and don't need the white outline that the current icons use to stand out. The icons are shots of the actual 3D objects (just like now) but I'm spending more time lighting them and making sure they look sharp. Also getting rid of the transparency should help performance a bit. And the new font is way more readable and less boring than the current default font.

Of note, the compass is being replaced with the new look in the upper right. This will also help performance as the current compass is basically a second camera. You'll also notice the quests look a bit different too, with the main quest open and the other two collapsed. Tabbing between quests will open the active quest.

Not pictured, but I'm also working on some smaller updates to make the UI more controller friendly (especially for pop-up information) and using the tabs in the build menu. So the changes aren't just the aesthetics.

This is all still in progress (the shots above are mock-ups) and I'll be working on this in the background while I continue to fix and optimize stuff.

I hope everyone is staying safe and healthy... and as always, thank you so much for the support!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

Beta 7.5 adds the memory optimization we were testing in the test build along with improved performance for lower spec computers and some other big fixes. The memory optimization reduced the initial memory that HammerHelm needs when loading. This was a really big update to how HammerHelm loaded objects like trees and buildings into the scene so I wanted to be sure and test it thoroughly.

In addition to the memory optimization, I also optimized the trees used when set at the lowest setting. This should provide a performance boost for those playing on lower spec computers. I'm likely going to try something similar with the other trees to improve performance at all tree settings.

This update also includes some fixes:
[list][*]The map UI can no longer be opened with other UI are already open.
[*]Footstep sounds now correctly play when on the Haunted Island.
[*]Fixed the collision for the small stone wall, allowing you to walk on top of it like the other walls.[/list]
-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: Test Build Beta 7.4 - Memory Optimization
notes.content:
Today's build has a big update to the way HammerHelm uses memory. Things have been a bit quiet lately as I've been working on this and it's a big change. 

It's a new way of loading assets like the trees and buildings. This optimization cuts the initial memory use of HammerHelm by about 50%!

Because it affects loading the town, I've uploaded a test build before launching this to the live branch.

If you would like to check out the system, you can get it by doing the following:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - MemoryTest2020 - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

You shouldn't notice much of a difference other than the initial load takes a bit longer. After that, loading your town and placing new buildings should be fast.

I'm going to spend more time testing this and hope to launch it on Sunday unless we find any problems.

To get back to the live build:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

Thanks everyone!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: Beta 7.3 - Meaningful Moods and More
notes.content:
The Meaningful Moods update is here! Better mood tracking, more effects (both good and bad) for moods, and a bunch of other changes. 

[i]All times mentioned below are in-game time.[/i]

[h3][b]Mood Tracking[/b][/h3]
In addition to seeing the mood lists from the Townspeople Manager menu, you can view an individual Dwarf's mood buffs and debuffs though the conversation menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/cf3c632297a98268fec927ad363ac939c258780a.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Mood Buff and Debuff Changes[/b][/h3]
[b]Mood Calculation:[/b] The overall calculation for mood has been updated so that higher moods are a bit easier to achieve.

[b]Town Status Moods:[/b] Townspeople now start with three negative moods, lack of water, town is dirty, and town is ugly. Existing townspeople (from loading a save prior to this update) will have these moods unless their homes are buffed from structures. Placing sewers, wells, and beauty related structures will remove these debuffs and replace them with the mood buff, creating a nice overall boost in mood.

[b]Starting Mood Increase:[/b] Because Dwarves will start with three negative moods, the "I just moved here" mood has been increased from +20 to +50. This buff also lasts twice as long - four in-game days. Over time the buff amount from this mood decreases for new townspeople down to 20. This gives you a chance to build structures that affect mood without the initial "I just moved here" mood buff being too high once you have built mood structures in the mid to later stages of the game. Note, this change only affects newly arriving Dwarves. So, if you load a save with existing Dwarves they'll still be set using the current mood buff from "I just moved here".

[b]Grumpy:[/b] The mood debuff from the "grumpy" trait has been reduced from -15 to -10.

[b]Beauty:[/b] The mood buff from beauty has been increased from +5 to +10 to match the other structure related mood buffs.

[b]Death:[/b] Dying now resets the timer on the "champion died" debuff back to one full in-game day. This makes death a bit more meaningful, but not crushing.

[b]Mood Effects, Good and Bad[/b]
A Dwarf's mood affects a lot more things, both good and bad.

[b]Resource Gathering:[/b] High mood increases the amount of resources (wood, stone, leather, etc.) a Dwarf drops off at the storehouse. Low mood can reduce this amount.

[b]Town Crafting:[/b] High mood increases the amount of crafted items (meals, clothing, tools, etc.) a Dwarf can make for the town. The additional craftables do not consume more resources. Low mood can reduce this amount. 

[b]Master-crafted and Poor:[/b] High mood increases the chance of a "master-crafted" item if the Dwarf has the "meticulous" trait. Low mood increases the chance of a "poor" item, even if the Dwarf isn't "clumsy". Low mood will also mean a "meticulous" Dwarf will not craft anything "master-crafted".

[h3][b]House Upgrades[/b][/h3]
[b]Sustained Mood:[/b] If the homeowners of a house both have sustained good mood for one in-game day, their house will upgrade to include planter boxes outside. Once this occurs, the planter boxes remain even if one or both of the homeowners has their mood lowered. This timer is paused during the Orc Quest so you don't lose momentum towards this goal. When a house or houses are upgraded in this way you will receive an alert.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/c6c49bc722713cd12950a3a2a3a4b65dc4c6aa95.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Other Updates[/b][/h3]
This update also includes the following:
[list][*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused workers to forget to build a structure.
[*]Reduced the number of trees that spawn when using the two lowest tree settings. This helps improve performance while still allowing the forest to look full.
[*]Replaced the jump animation when standing still.
[*]Added invisible walls around the island to prevent the character from going underwater. I might add a swim animation at some point, but there really isn't any point to going in the ocean so the walls prevent the weird teleport back to town system I was previously using.
[*]Replaced the Metalworkers axe with the new axe (they were still using the old one).
[*]Updated the animations in the title screen to use the new townspeople animations.[/list]
Thank you again everyone for all of your feedback and support!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
jon@hammerhelm.com
[list][*]My Twitter: https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios
[*]Discord Channel: discord.gg/soedesco[/list]

notes.title: WIP - Meaningful Moods

Right now, townspeople mood doesn't have a big impact on gameplay and there isn't any real reason to try to increase townspeople mood. I'm working on an update to change that!

The Meaningful Moods update will include more effects for high and low mood in addition to a permanent NPC house upgrade for sustained good mood. [i]Note all times mentioned below are in-game time.[/i]

[b]Mood Tracking[/b]
In addition to seeing the mood lists from the Townspeople Manager menu, you will be able to view an individual Dwarf's mood buffs and debuffs though the conversation menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/cf3c632297a98268fec927ad363ac939c258780a.jpg[/img]

[b]Mood Buff and Debuff Changes[/b]
The overall calculation for mood will be changed so that higher moods are a bit easier to achieve.

Townspeople will start with three negative moods, lack of water, town is dirty, and town is ugly. Right now, placing water wells, sewers, and beauty related decor only gives a positive mood buff, but there was never a negative mood for not having those things. Existing townspeople (from loading a save prior to this update) will have these moods unless their homes are buffed from structures.

To counter-act this in the early game, the "I just moved here" mood will be increased from +20 to +50. This buff will also last twice as long - four in-game days. Over time the buff amount from this mood will decrease for new townspeople down to 20. This gives you a chance to build structures that affect mood without the initial "I just moved here" mood buff being too high once you have built mood structures in the mid to later stages of the game. Note, this change will only affect newly arriving Dwarves once the update is live. So, if you load a save with existing Dwarves they'll still be set using the current mood buff from "I just moved here".

The mood debuff from the "grumpy" trait will be reduced from -15 to -10.

The mood buff from beauty will be increased from +5 to +10 to match the other structure related mood buffs.

Dying will reset the timer on the "champion died" debuff back to one full in-game day. Right now, it doesn't affect the timer - so if you die and then 23 in-game hours later die again, the mood debuff only lasts one in-game hour. Resetting it to 24 in-game hours makes death a bit more meaningful, but not crushing.

[b]Mood Effects, Good and Bad[/b]
A Dwarf's mood will affect a lot more things, both good and bad.

High mood will increase the amount of resources (wood, stone, leather, etc.) a Dwarf drops off at the storehouse. Low mood can reduce this amount.

High mood will increase the amount of crafted items (meals, clothing, tools, etc.) a Dwarf can make for the town. The additional craftables do not consume more resources. Low mood can reduce this amount. 

High mood will increase the chance of a "master-crafted" item if the Dwarf has the "meticulous" trait. Low mood increases the chance of a "poor" item, even if the Dwarf isn't "clumsy". Low mood will also mean a "meticulous" Dwarf will not craft anything "master-crafted".

If the homeowners of a house both have sustained good mood for one in-game day, their house will upgrade to include planter boxes outside. Once this occurs, the planter boxes remain even if one of the homeowners has their mood lowered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/c6c49bc722713cd12950a3a2a3a4b65dc4c6aa95.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Beta 7.0 - Townspeople Animations, Combat Balance, and more
notes.content:
A big update tonight that includes the new townspeople animations, some combat balance, and a host of other fixes and improvements!

[u][b]Townspeople Animations[/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/71b4af97841fda288876772cb934d1b1a833d5a7.gif[/img]

Townspeople now perform different animations depending on what they are carrying.
[list][*]Fishermen, Miners, and Farmers deliver their goods to the storehouse carrying a couple of baskets.
[*]Workers have an animation to carry a stone or log rather than it appearing on their back.
[*]Fishermen have a fishing animation when they are at the dock.
[*]Farmers and Fishermen have different walk and run animations that has them carrying their tool on their shoulder.
[*]All townspeople have a new standard run animation. The old one didn't look good to me.[/list]
I'm super happy with how these turned out as these animations are a lot nicer and more varied than the previous set. The town feels way more alive! I'm probably going to add storehouse drop-offs to some of the other jobs as seeing the Dwarves delivering goods with the new animations just looks really cool.

[u][b]Combat Balance[/b][/u]
Attack animations have been sped up about 20%. They looked too slow to me, almost as if the character was fighting underwater. Monster hit points have been increased about 15% for monsters spawned after the tutorial. The net effect of this is fights should take about the same amount of time since you are hitting faster, but should look and feel a lot better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29603119/c17757f5a445d948eb0514490adc489d7baf942d.gif[/img]

Note the gif looks a bit faster than it actually is since it's a low framerate. I'm probably going to change how and when monsters decide to attack as there are still a bit too many times where they are killed and never attack. I didn't want to make that change at the same time that I made the speed and hit-points changes though.

[u][b]Improvements and Balance[/b][/u]
[list][*]Adjusted the terrain towards the back of the island to reduce the height of the mountains. This allows me to optimize performance a bit by turning them off when you are far away. Lowering them a bit means you won't see them "pop in" when they are loaded.
[*]Added a check to keep the game from saving if the load didn't finish properly. This is a stop-gap just in case a load fails to ensure the game doesn't then save over it and corrupt the save. Hopefully not something that will ever be needed, but safe is better than sorry!
[*]Changed the prerequisite for the Grrumble quest so you can get his quest earlier.
[*]Increased the debuff from the "bad day", "got in a fight", "ate too much", and "drank too much" events.
[*]Townspeople who have resources and attempt to deliver them to the storehouse will drop those resources before returning to their home.[/list]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list][*]Fixed a couple of bugs related to stacked items and the "Loot All" button in the treasure chest menu. It will now correctly fill in any existing stacks (up to 64) before creating a new stack if there are any remaining.
[*]Fixed another loot bug related to moving stacks of items around.
[*]Farmers will now run back to their farm after dropping off their food at the storehouse rather than walk. They should only walk when tending their crops.
[*]Replaced the torches in the sewers and on the Orc map as they were old and causing problems after I updated to the latest Unity version.
[*]Fixed a bug related to localizing the Tavernkeeper and Tinker.
[*]Fixed a bug relating to the "Turn Off Furniture" button for Carpenters and Stonemasons.[/list]

This was a really fun update to put together after spending so much time on controller support and localization. Next up I need to focus on something that will lower the initial memory footprint and speed up the initial load time a bit. After that I'd like to either add some more quests that I've designed and look for more opportunities to optimize the game more.

Thank you again everyone for all of your support and feedback!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
jon@hammerhelm.com
[list][*]My Twitter: https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios
[*]Discord Channel: discord.gg/soedesco[/list]
