notes.title: Quick Roadmap Update
notes.content:
I've been going over this bullet point from my roadmap:
[h1][list][*]Add more meaningful events for the townspeople.[/h1]
and decided to change it a bit. Originally the idea here was that a "sleepy" townsperson might go home and go to bed or a "lazy" townsperson might leave their shop and go for a walk. In theory, I thought it would add some falvor to the town, but in practice I think it would be super annoying to have to hunt down a armorsmith if s/he decided to take a nap. And if you happened to miss the message about it, you wouldn't know to even look!

I was about to announce that I was scrapping it for now, but then had an idea and worked on it and so far I like it.

The new system still uses the townspeople traits when deciding whether something happens or not, but keeps the Dwarf on the job so to speak. 

So a Dwarf with the "happy" trait might get a mood buff because s/he "had a great day". In addition, a Dwarf with the "happy" trait might also cheer up another Dwarf - and they BOTH get a mood buff. So happy Dwarves can be very useful.

Likewise a "grumpy" Dwarf is more likely to have a bad day and might even insult another Dwarf, giving that Dwarf a slight mood debuff. Having the "grumpy" Dwarf get a mood buff from doing this might be kinda funny too.

Other ideas include a Drunkard going on a drinking binge, which uses up more beer and gives them a slight mood debuff.

And a sleepy Dwarf complaining about being tired (again with a mood debuff)

And a brawler Dwarf might start a fight with another Dwarf. The Brawler actually gets a mood buff from this, while the other Dwarf gets a mood debuff, since they didn't want to fight. Unless - the other Dwarf also has the Brawler trait, in which case they'd BOTH get a mood buff. And a Dwarf with the "Pacifist" trait would get a bigger mood debuff since they detest fighting more than a normal Dwarf.

Lots of things here. Mostly to add flavor but also to make the Dwarf traits more meaningful and impactful.

I also kind of like the idea of allowing you to talk to a Dwarf who has a negative mood from one of these events and cheer them back up, thus removing the debuff and turning it around into a positive thing. In this case, since the town Champion went out of their way to help the Dwarf out, that Dwarf might get an additional benefit such as a walk speed increase, carrying more resources, or a higher chance to make a Masterwork item. This might also give you a bit of XP and/or maybe a bit of gold. 

When one of these things happens, an alert will appear. But these aren't quests and you don't HAVE to do anything about them. They're purely optional as the mood buffs and debuffs only last for a short period of time and go away on their own. If I do the part of the system that lets you intervene I'll also come up with some way to easily identify a Dwarf that you can cheer up.

I just finished the initial system and it seems fun so far. I'm adding in all of the various events based on the traits now.

notes.title: Optimization Test Build
notes.content:
I've created a test build of the new optimizations! 

Right now they mostly work best when you have a large town. The optimizations don't do a lot when you are facing a large expanse of the forest, but I expect to work on that part once I change out the environment art. 

And you should notice a big improvement to performance when you are inside of a building.

You can toggle the performance optimization system on and off by pressing F1 to see if you notice a difference. When you load a fresh game, the default is ON.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/a84939f5cac040e0f64fb0f12f288abaab7b654e.gif[/img]

Note you'll notice in the above .gif that the characters don't turn off. In this updated version, they do however!

On my development laptop I saw a framerate jump of about 20-30% when looking from one end of a large town to the other end. When inside a building it was even higher than that. 

On my low-spec machine the benefits weren't as great, so I'm going to be working on more options in the settings screen to improve framerate for lower-spec computers in addition to this optimization system.

If you'd like to try it out, you can get the test build by doing this...

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - PerfTest2019 - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game.

To get back to the Alpha client:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

notes.title: Alpha 12.7 - Monster Bug Fix and Grrrumble Update
notes.content:
Small update tonight but it includes a HUGE fix for the monster bug I mentioned in an earlier announcement.

Monsters who took damage from dash attacks and acid weapons would get confused and try to attack the acid (the thing that was hurting them) rather than the player. This caused all sorts of problems, including making monsters invulnerable, making them run away from you (trying to find the acid!) and making quest completes fail.

I've turned off the elemental effects for weapons for now. I'm probably going to redo them sometime soon. Took me all night to find this one and I want to thank those that posted the bug and sent the log files!

This update also includes a change to the Grrrumble quest. The quest is no longer rare and should appear as a normal Story Quest once you have a Stonemason.

Grrrumble is also sporting the new Copper Ram Helmet. Sorry, he gets it before you do. Look at him...he's a huge Earth Elemental, how am I supposed to tell him "no"?! :)

notes.title: Alpha 12.5 - More Bug Fixes!
notes.content:
Spent some more time fixing bugs this evening. Tonight's build includes a bunch of Orc Quest fixes as well as some others.
[list][*]The Skeletons during the Orc quest will no longer spawn in places where they cannot be found.
[*]Orcs will always have a greeting of some kind rather than having a blank conversation box.
[*]While on Orc Island, you can no longer press the Build Mode tabs to see Dwarf buildings in the build list.
[*]Likewise, Orc buildings will no longer appear in town build list after returning from Orc Island
[*]Orc health and stamina bars no longer cover up hit point and stamina numbers.
[*]Orc Archers no longer have a crafting option since they don't craft anything.
[*]You can now use Fitted, Masterwork, and Poor quality items to craft the armor sets
[*]Using the town resource menu to transfer stone from the town to yourself will no longer give you two stone for every one in the town. ([b]bad bug!!![/b])
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Build Mode information panel to fail to display all of the text.
[*]Updated me email in the welcome message to use jon@hammerhelm.com
[/list]
edit: added these two fixes in Alpha 12.5.1
[list][*]Placing an item over a gem in a storage chest will no longer result in the gem being deleted.
[*]You can no longer collect the glowberries from the Herbalist's garden.[/list]

There are also a couple of bugs that I am aware of, but haven't been able to reproduce myself yet.
[list][*]Sometimes attacking a monster will always result in a miss when it should have hit.
[*]Workers sometimes get stuck in a loop, running around in a circle.[/list]
Both of these can be fixed by restarting the game, but if either does happen, please send me your save and your outpit_log file before restarting the game. These two have eluded me so far and I really want to knock them out.

You can find info on how to send me the files here:
https://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/1/1736595227848425568/

Again, and I can't say this enough, I really appreciate the bug reports. I've been playing this game for so long I often miss things because when I play, I play it the way I expect it to be played. But that's an illusion that never holds up once people get their hands on it. It's always fascinating to me read a bug report and think "Why would you do that!?" - and then figure it out and fix it. :)

Focusing on bugs has also been really helpful for me to gauge HammerHelm's overall polish. As I fix bugs I also make note of things that aren't necessarily broken, but could be improved or made more fun. That's where the idea for new building animation I showed the other day came from.

https://steamcommunity.com/games/664000/announcements/detail/1647664350689507667
Meanwhile the artists continue to work on the new weapons and armor. The Copper Armor and Copper Weapons are ready for review so I'll probably show them tomorrow if they look good once in the game. The Jade Armor and Weapons need some rework as getting the Jade looking good has been tricky. He's also made some progress on the Zombie too, so hoping to show his work-in-progress soon. Lots going on!

Also, that something special I mentioned in the roadmap update is also ready for review. Can't wait to check it out. Again, it's not a huge thing, but it's special to me, and I hope you all like it.

notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9dc2bad32061c792b24af6281adaa45747e3b216.jpg[/img]

It's always nice to be able to mark something as done in the roadmap list, even better when it's three things! The Fast Travel system, additional uses for Alchemy Ingredients, and additional Steam Achievements are done!

If you haven't read the original Roadmap announcement I recommend reading it at the link below. It provides a lot of context for the stuff on the list:

https://steamcommunity.com/games/664000/announcements/detail/1710706508279875941
I've also included some images and links to some of the more recent updates for those of you who are just finding HammerHelm so you can see the newly added and upcoming stuff that is listed in the In Progress Section!

Below is a list of the goals and the progress that has been made on them so far.

Note when something says "Done" that doesn't mean I'll never add more to it, it simply means I'm happy with where it is for now and moving on to other things. After leaving early access I will very likely come back to many of these to add more to them or make changes to improve them. 

[h1]IN PROGRESS[/h1]
[list]
[*][h1][b]Replace the placeholder monsters.[/b][/h1]
- Almost all of the new monsters are done, with just two remaining. They  have concepts and the 3D artist is working on the models. He's currently focused on the weapons and armor though so expect this to remain "in progress" for a while.
[*][h1][b]Replace the placeholder weapons and armor.[/b][/h1]
- All weapons and armor have concept art. 3D modeling has started. This has been a bit slow going as the artist and I dial in the models and textures.
[*][h1][b]Replace the placeholder trees and flora.[/b][/h1]
- The large trees are done as are the small trees, bushes, rocks, and flowers. I'm hoping to start reworking the world map soon.
[*][h1][b]Controller support.[/b][/h1]
- Support for character controls is done. Movement, combat and quests are working, as is looting, inventory, and skill points. Basically the core gameplay of adventuring works with a controller. I have some more UI updated to support the controller as well and those will be in the next update.
[*][h1][b]More quests.[/b][/h1]
- In Progress. Let's just say this will never be "done". :) I have added a bunch of new quests and will continue to add more. The sewer map has also been updated and not only looks better, but is also set up for more quests.[/list]

[h1]DONE[/h1]
[*][h1][b]Add character skills system.[/b][/h1]
- Done and released in build 9.3!
[*][h1][b]Add some more life to the town.[/b][/h1]
- Done, implemented in 11.3. Implemented "town wandering" for Workers and Shopkeeper activities. I plan on adding more shopkeepers to this, but so far the Alchemist and Herbalist are both using it.
[*][h1][b]Alerts for when your town is low on a resource and other important messaging.[/b][/h1]
- Done, released in Alpha 9.4!
[*][h1][b]More customization.[/b][/h1]
- Done! Added skin tone options and new tunic colors. I'll probably add more things as well but for now I'm happy with the character customization.
[*][h1][b]Add some more items to place in your home.[/b][/h1]
- Done. Added monster head trophies. Will also remake the armor and weapon decor once the new armor and weapons are in.
[*][h1][b]Add some kind of fast travel system[/b][/h1]
- Done! Teleport Plaforms and Teleport Crystals added.
[*][h1][b]Add some more uses for alchemy ingredients other than potions.[/b][/h1]
- Added alchemy to the tunic dying system in Alpha 10.1. Also added alchemy resources as ingredients in crafting Teleport Crystals.
[*][h1][b]Add some more Steam Achievements.[/b][/h1]
- Added a few more based on recently added content.
[*][h1][b]Make a new HammerHelm logo.[/b][/h1]
- Done![/list]

[h1]NOT STARTED YET[/h1]
[*][h1][b]Add a few more points of interest to the map.[/b][/h1]
- I'll likely do this while I update the world map.
[*][h1][b]Add more meaningful events for the townspeople.[/b][/h1]
- I'm actually debating whether I want to do this or not as having shopkeepers leave their shop might be kind of annoying. Going to give this some more thought.[/list]

As you can see most of the major remaining work is art related. So that leaves me time to work on some other things while the artists wrap up their projects.

I mentioned these in the previous roadmap update but will list them here as well since they are still ongoing.
[list][*]New sound effects for the Fire and Ice Elementals, so they won't sound the same as the Earth Elementals. If this goes well, I might have some more sounds made as well.
[*]Some more new trees, including the cherry blossoms, weeping willows, and a pine tree.
[*]Some more quests for Grrrumble. I really like this character and want to expand on him more. Also hoping to add some more special characters, but those will likely be after leaving early access.
[*]And something special that I don't want to talk about just yet. It's not a big thing, but it's something special to me and I hope you like it. Should be able to show it in about a week.[/list]

I'm still not quite ready to post a date for leaving early access, but I'd say we're definitely looking good for 2019, likely during the fall and maybe before! I think it's going to mostly come down to how quickly the new art is completed. If the art does take a while longer that just means I have more time to add and improve stuff! ːsteamhappyː

As always, if you have any questions, comments, or feedback I'd love to hear it!

notes.title: Alpha 12.3 - Teleport Platforms
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/60854f1dfa178edaeab99aa248ce6e52b6c69d6c.jpg[/img]
Today's build includes the new Teleport Platforms that I've mentioned over the past few days. I've made a few changes to how they work.
[list][*]Teleport Platforms are crafted and placed using the same building menu as other town structures.
[*]You must have a Stonemason to place a Teleport Platform.
[*]Once placed, you can use teleport crystals to teleport back to your town.
[*]Teleport crystals come in 4 varieties, Jade, Gold, Diamond, and Blood Stone.
[*]A Teleport Platform has 6 "charges" per day. Each of the four teleport crystals uses a different amount of charges. Jade = 6, Gold = 3, Diamond = 2, and Bloodstone = 1.
[*]Jade and Gold teleport crystals can be crafted at the Stonemason using Jade or Gold Ingots and alchemy ingredients.
[*]Diamond and Bloodstone teleport crystals are crafted at the Mage using Diamond or Blood Stone Ingots and alchemy ingredients.[/list]
You cannot use a teleport crystal if:
[list][*]You are inside the town perimeter already.
[*]You are in a cave, dungeon or other underground location.
[*]You are standing at a dungeon, cave, or other entrance.
[*]You are drinking a potion.
[*]You are dead. :)
[*]You have any UI open such as inventory, crafting, ESC menu, etc.
[*]You are not a Dwarf or are not on the main island (this will make sense once you get a certain quest :P)
[*]You are standing near a treasure chest.[/list]
Based on feedback I might add some more limitations to using the crystals.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/4a9a38aa93b65266b56f222f021ed26c38acb733.gif[/img]

If you try to use a teleport crystal while the Teleport Platform doesn't have enough charges left for the day, you will get a message letting you know how many charges the Teleport Platform has.

Right now using a teleport crystal teleports your immediately. I might add a small delay with an animation, but I wanted to get this system out in a build so you all could try it out.

notes.title: Roadmap to Full Release Progress Update
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9dc2bad32061c792b24af6281adaa45747e3b216.jpg[/img]

Time for another Development Update on the Road to Full Release. You can read the original Roadmap Announcement here:

https://steamcommunity.com/games/664000/announcements/detail/1710706508279875941
Below is a list of the goals and the progress that has been made on them so far.

Note when something says "Done" that doesn't mean I'll never add more to it, it simply means I'm happy with where it is for now and moving on to other things. After leaving early access I will very likely come back to many of these to add more to them or make changes to improve them. 

Also, changing the format of this to hopefully make it easier to read.

[h1]IN PROGRESS[/h1]
[list]
[*][h1][b]Replace the placeholder monsters.[/b][/h1]
- Almost all of the new monsters are done, with just two remaining. They  have concepts and the 3D artist is working on the models. He's currently focused on the weapons and armor though so expect this to remain "in progress" for a while.
[*][h1][b]Replace the placeholder weapons and armor.[/b][/h1]
- All weapons and armor have concept art. 3D modeling has started. I should have some 3D models to show soon!
[*][h1][b]Replace the placeholder trees and flora.[/b][/h1]
- The large trees are done as are the small trees, bushes, rocks, and flowers. Updating the map itself with all of these new assets is going to be a big undertaking but I hope to start on it soon.
[*][h1][b]Add some more uses for alchemy ingredients other than potions.[/b][/h1]
- In progress. Added alchemy to the tunic dying system in Alpha 10.1. I'm not sure if I'll add more before leaving EA, but for now calling this in progress rather than done.
[*][h1][b]Controller support.[/b][/h1]
- Support for character controls is done. Movement, combat and quests are working, as is looting, inventory, and skill points. Basically the core gameplay of adventuring works with a controller. I still need to add building placement, crafting, and the other various UI. Big undertaking!
[*][h1][b]Add some kind of fast travel system[/b][/h1]
- In progress. I have the teleport platform and teleport stones working. Now I need to decide how and where you can go on the map.
[*][h1][b]More quests.[/b][/h1]
- In Progress. Let's just say this will never be "done". :) I have added a bunch of new quests and will continue to add more. The sewer map has also been updated and not only looks better, but is also set up for more quests.[/list]

[h1]DONE[/h1]
[*][h1][b]Add character skills system.[/b][/h1]
- Done and released in build 9.3!
[*][h1][b]Add some more life to the town.[/b][/h1]
- Done, implemented in 11.3. Implemented "town wandering" for Workers and Shopkeeper activities. I plan on adding more shopkeepers to this, but so far the Alchemist and Herbalist are both using it.
[*][h1][b]Alerts for when your town is low on a resource and other important messaging.[/b][/h1]
- Done, released in Alpha 9.4!
[*][h1][b]More customization.[/b][/h1]
- Done! Added skin tone options and new tunic colors. I'll probably add more things as well but for now I'm happy with the character customization.
[*][h1][b]Add some more items to place in your home.[/b][/h1]
- Done. Added monster head trophies. Will also remake the armor and weapon decor once the new armor and weapons are in.
[*][h1][b]Make a new HammerHelm logo.[/b][/h1]
- Done![/list]

[h1]NOT STARTED YET[/h1]
[*][h1][b]Add a few more points of interest to the map.[/b][/h1]
- Not started yet.
[*][h1][b]Add more meaningful events for the townspeople.[/b][/h1]
- Not started yet.
[*][h1][b]Add some more Steam Achievements.[/b][/h1]
- Have a list but haven't started development yet.[/list]

The DONE section keeps getting bigger while the NOT STARTED YET section is down to just three things. ːsteamhappyː I really appreciate the feedback on all of the updates and hope you are enjoying seeing them as much as I am enjoying making them!

In addition to everything above, I also have some other things in progress:
[list][*]New sound effects for the Fire and Ice Elementals, so they won't sound the same as the Earth Elementals. If this goes well, I might have some more sounds made as well.
[*]Some more new trees, including the cherry blossoms, weeping willows, and a pine tree.
[*]Some more quests for Grrrumble. I really like this character and want to expand on him more. Also hoping to add some more special characters, but those will likely be after leaving early access.
[*]And something special that I don't want to talk about just yet. It's not a big thing, but it's something special to me and I hope you like it.[/list]
I'm not quite ready to post a date for leaving early access just yet, but based on the above lists I think we're getting close. The largest undertakings are going to be redoing the world map, finishing controller support, and getting all of the new art completed and set up in game. So don't quote me on this, but I'm hoping for some time this summer or early fall. We'll see how things progress, but I think it's safe to say that barring something unforeseen, we're on track for sometime this year!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
Founder and Developer, SuperSixStudios
- jon@hammerhelm.com
- https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios

notes.content:
[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/5fc993445b506143ea2c69e316b59dab864857b6.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/5fc993445b506143ea2c69e316b59dab864857b6.jpg[/img][/url]

I wasn't planning on showing anything related to the new world map and the new environment assets, since I'm still a ways away from actually changing them all out in the game, but I'm so happy with how this turned out I had to share.

This is visual target piece I put together to give myself a goal for what the game world will look like when I update it. Also called a "beautiful corner". It's not optimized, but it provides a template for how I want the world to look when I change out all of the environment art.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/0f01bc5352bb3b61020cca7d70e7ae8d1576dfb7.gif[/img]

Note the falling leaves particle, the trees swaying in the wind, the smaller plants and flowers, and the rocks, which have a small bit of moss on them. Lots of configuration options like the color of the leaves, the amount of moss on the rocks, etc. so I can create lots of variety. The flowers are neat because they aren't flat like the grass, they're actual models that have some depth to them. It's difficult to tell in the gif, but the flowers and bushes are also moving with the wind.

As I said before, it's going to be a while before the game looks like this. I think the trees and other assets match the characters and monsters much better than the current place-holder assets. 

I'm very happy with how the beautiful corner turned out and I hope you like it too!

notes.title: Alpha 10.6 - Improvements and Fixes
notes.content:
Today's build includes a bunch of improvements, slight balance tweaks, and fixes.
[list][*]You can now use the controller to skip through the introduction windows by pressing A.
[*]Fixed a bug related to using the controller and the inventory screen.
[*]Fixed a bug related to the "Strange Activity" quest when it involves the sewers.
[*]Improved the quest pointer for the Strange Activity Quest.
[*]You cannot use the names "Shaydee", "Ghost", or "Grrrumble" for NPC names. Doing this can cause an error. I'm going to update the code so it doesn't break if you use those names as I don't want to have to add new names every time I make a new character.
[*]Adjusted the balance for the skills system. Most skills were slightly reduced. Second Wind was slightly improved.
[*]If you get a bunch of different loot from a treasure chest, the Luck skill will now only work on one of them. This will remove the overhead text spam.
[*]Fixed a bug with the Carpenter building that would sometimes cause your character to get pushed into the air.
[*]Fixed a bug related to loading a save when you have the "Rats in the Cellar" quest.[/list]
I'm also making good progress on getting the elementals set up and a new quest. I'm hoping to release a build for them this weekend!

notes.title: Alpha 10.5 - UI and Combat Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Today's update includes a bunch of bug fixes, some related to the UI update and a few related to combat.
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused the Enter Mines UI to fail to let you into the mines.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the power attack gems to disappear when you could perform a power attack.
[*]Fixed a bug that would sometimes cause the power attack to fail to work even when you had all three gems.
[*]Swinging and missing will now play the miss sound again.
[*]Reworked the alerts system so they will no longer remain on the screen indefinitely.
[*]Fixed a few minor UI scaling issues.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused monsters to not take damage when hit.[/list]
That last bug is one that I could not personally reproduce, but it was reported by a few people. I believe I found the code responsible for the bug, but if this happens to you after this build please let me know and send me your output_log file if you can.

https://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/1/1736595227848425568/

[h1]Also, I want to apologize for the bugs in the last couple of days. The UI scaling update caused a bunch of unexpected errors, a number of which I really should have caught. One step forward and two steps back isn't fun.[/h1]

I'm going to spend the next couple of days focusing on play testing and looking for anymore UI related bugs before I spend time adding the new monsters and other new content.

I very much appreciate the support and feedback and I'm very excited to move towards full release, but sometimes It's good to slow down a bit before moving forward!

notes.title: Alpha 10.3 - Town Related Updates
notes.content:
A quick build tonight to add a new feature for townspeople homes and fix a couple of town related bugs.

One of the things I hear a lot from people when they first play HammerHelm is they don't realize that the townspeople homes can be furnished. You place a house and walk inside and it's empty! Kind of a letdown if you don't know they can have furniture. 

So when placing a house, the furniture that hasn't been built yet will appear as "ghosted" placeholders. As furniture is crafted and placed, the new furniture replaces the placeholder.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9ef2ffbfeef7c270afb7bf44695ce2586431d9a2.jpg[/img]

A the two bug fixes:
[list][*]Carpenters will no longer drop their quality wood when they aren't ready to craft. This could cause the Carpenter to get confused after returning from the Storehouse with Quality Wood.
[*]The Town Management UI arrows to switch between the NPC list and the resource list will now correctly work. I broke this when I added the extra information to the Townspeople traits.[/list]
I'm still working on getting the Fire and Ice Elementals set up and the Stone Elemental is still in progress as well. Once he's done I'll get them all in the game.

I also got the new environment art back from the 3D artist. There's a lot! A new tree (to add to the previous three), new rocks, new flowers, some bushes, etc. It's like digital Christmas in March! :)  

It's going to take me a while to redo the world map with the new assets, but I'll likely create a "visual goal" test using all of the new art so you can see how the game will look when it's all in.

notes.title: Alpha 10.1 - Tunic Dyes and Tweaks
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/c599b863c6d8fa9b9f92775c7cf26d28b9c9835c.png[/img]

Tonight's update includes the Tunic Dye system and some small tweaks. 

You all seemed to like the Tunic Dye idea so much (based on the likes the announcement got!) that I decided to finish it and get it in the game!

You can craft clothing dyes at the Tailor using Alchemy ingredients. I'm still tweaking the balance for these so the recipes might change.

There are two new colors (black and yellow) that are only available through the Tailor. I'll likely add some more and perhaps some two-tone colors too. I'll also be making a few of the colors exclusive to Early Access supporters. More on that at a future date.

This build also includes some bug fixes and tweaks:
[list][*]Monster Head Trophies now display in the crafting preview window.
[*]Right-clicking to unequip an item now correctly sets your stats.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused right-clicking to unequip an item to not remove the 3D object for that item on your character.
[*]The green controller selection indicator for the NPC Conversation UI now defaults to off until you make a controller input.
[*]Increased the minimum number of placed buildings before Workers will begin to wander a town. At only four buildings it just looked weird. The new minimum is seven and I might increase it further depending on how that feels.[/list]
Work continues on the new monsters. We're working on an updated texture for the Fire Elemental to make him match better with the other monsters and the Earth Elemental is almost modeled as well. The same artist is also working on the new weapons and armor.

Once all three Elementals are done I'll probably put them in the game rather than wait for the other monsters to finish up. That might take too long, plus I need them for some quests I'm working on!

notes.title: Alpha 10.0 - Monster Trophies, Balance, and Bug Fixes
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/dcc3888a12970a17c9973f26072cd421b0dac314.jpg[/img]

Monsters will now sometimes drop "monster parts" that can be used to craft monster head trophies at the Tailor! These trophies can be placed in your home.

Orcs, Goblins, Skeletons, Ratmen, and MushroomMen are available now. The other monsters will become available once I add the new models to the game.

It might be difficult to get the lower level monsters if you are playing with a high level character. I'm going to work on something that makes the lower level monster parts available in the loot table when your character is at higher levels.

notes.title: Alpha 9.7 - Controller Support + Ice Elemental WIP
notes.content:
Today's build includes the first and second phases of adding controller support to HammerHelm. It also includes some bugs fixes, so I'll start with those first and then explain the controller stuff.
[list][*]The power attack UI will now correctly reset after you use your power attack.
[*]The second and third "How to Fight" screens can now be closed with the ESC key (I did this as part of controller support)
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the message that a tree cannot be chopped down because it isn't fully grown when you weren't hitting a tree.
[*]Updated all of the grass on the world map to use the new color and varied positioning.
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the quest manager to give you an Orc quest after you've already completed the Orc Quest.
[*]The Orc Hut should no longer appear in the "Homes" tab when in your town.
[/list]
Ok, now on to controller support!

This build includes controller support for the main menu screens (except the settings UI) and for character movement, combat, and the hot-bar. You can also close any UI with the controller, however the game windows such as Inventory, Crafting, etc. are not supported yet. That's phase three.

When in the title screen you can use the d-pad to select options and the A button to select the highlighted option. The first time you use the d-pad, the green highlight indicator will appear. You can also press the B button to open the settings UI, however the options in that UI require the mouse to operate.

On character creation, you can move the d-pad left and right to change the options for hair, beards, etc. Moving the left stick right and left will spin the character.

In game, the controller works as follows:

Left Stick - move forward, backward, strafe left, strafe right
Right Stick - rotate left and right, look up and down
Press Left Stick - sprint
Left and Right Bumpers - roll left or right
Left stick down + either bumper - roll backwards
Right Trigger - press or press and hold to attack
Left Trigger - press and hold to block, release to stop blocking
Y - jump
B - perform power attack
A - Interact: this includes talking to NPCs, entering dungeons, opening treasure chests and virtually any other in-game action except opening the townspeople menu and the town building menu.
X - close UI (works the same as the ESC key)
D-pad left and right - select hotbar item
D-pad up or down - use hotbar item

The Dash attack isn't supported yet. I'll likely make it something like Left Stick up + B button.

One note regarding the A button. If you aren't near anything that you can interact with, pressing A will open your inventory.

While you can open UI using the controller, such as talking to an NPC, you cannot use the controller to navigate the NPC Conversation UI and equip items from your inventory. That'll be what I'm working on next.

I'm probably going to switch out the X button and make it so pressing X opens a new UI that allows you to either open the town building menu or the townspeople menu when you are in your town. The button to close UI would then switch to be the back button.

I'm still tweaking things with the controller, and I admit, I am more of a mouse-and-keyboard gamer, so I very much appreciate your feedback on it! Once everything is finalized I'll be adding a window to reference all of the controller controls.

I might take a break from controller work to implement some other features but the goal is to get all of the in-game windows to work with the controller other than entering text - which you only do once when you name your town.

And last, but not at all least, the environment and particle test for the Ice Elemental.

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7f29b0f1f9e41e60c84be42e1a9c781175b02b96.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7f29b0f1f9e41e60c84be42e1a9c781175b02b96.jpg[/img][/url]
[i](click to see full size image[/i]

He's pretty much done other than tweaking some animations. The Fire and Earth Elementals are in progress as well and work has also started on the new environment assets. Hope to show some of that in the coming weeks!

notes.title: Alpha 9.6 - Main Menu Controller Support
notes.content:
I've updated the test build with controller support for the main title screen menu! 
[list][*]Use the D-pad to cycle through the buttons or selections.
[*]Press A to activate a button.
[*]In the character selection screen you can use the D-pad to choose a character, make a new character, or delete a character.
[*]In character creation, pressing up or down on the D-pad highlights the various customization options, pressing right or left cycles through the options. Moving the right stick left or right turns the character.
Pressing X will close any window that has a Close button.
Pressing B while in the main menu will open the settings UI.
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/80c1cee807f411eae409e01565957dd857929ac1.gif[/img]

The only parts of the UI that are not set up for the controller are the settings screen and entering a character name. I might add a virtual keyboard at some point, but since you almost never enter text it'll likely be on the back-burner for a bit. Adding controller support to the settings UI will require a lot of re-writing of the system so I'm going to hold off on that for a while too. Again since it's not a UI that is used often I think that's ok for now.

Next up is to get controller support for all of the in-game UI such as inventory, craftng, looting, building, etc. That's going to be by far the largest undertaking. I'm probably going to work on some other things while I add controller support to those UI.

To get the test build:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - ControllerTest - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game.

To get back to the Alpha client:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

I've been playing around with the new trees for a while now and they're not quite where I want them, I'm happy with them overall so I wanted to show some progress.

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7d14f5ea59fdb43e1adbbacce3e2b7bb9b0d208e.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7d14f5ea59fdb43e1adbbacce3e2b7bb9b0d208e.jpg[/img][/url]

Really happy with the hand-painted look of these trees. I think they fit much better with the rest of the game. There are still some things I want to adjust though.

I think the leaves on the trees are a bit bright.  I like they way they look in low light but during mid day they're a little too bright. The red leaves especially need to be desaturated a bit. I'm also working on creating different shades of each leaf color so they're not always the same shade on every tree. 

The shots are just a one-to-one replacement of the current trees with the new trees, but because the canopy shapes are very different I'm going to need to move trees around to avoid areas of too much density.

The tree trunks are different shades of brown but I want to make the difference more obvious. Next up will be a couple of other trees including a birch tree to break up the look of the tree trunks even more. 

Once I have the trees looking the way I want I'll likely create a test build with them on the map that you all can try out!

In the first shot you'll note that the grass as more depth to it (it's not all one shade of green) and they aren't all facing the same direction. I think it looks better compared to the current grass.

I know I haven't released a new build in a bit now. I'll certainly be posting progress updates though and might make test "sneak peek" builds, so I hope you all enjoy seeing the progress!

notes.title: Alpha 9.3 - Skill System and Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Today's build includes the new Leveling and Skill System!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/8c91be0b343ed8eff2955a68fa650dd5d6c854df.gif[/img]

As you play the game your character will gain Skill Points. These points can be spent to obtain and upgrade skills. Each skill can be upgraded twice, creating three tiers for each skill counting the initial purchase.

Upgrading a skill will increase its chance to take effect and its potency. So for example, when initially purchased, "Tough Skin" reduces damage by 7%. Upgrading it will increase that to 14% and upgrading it again increases it to 21%.

Some skill are always on, such as Tough Skin, so it always reduced the damage. Other skills have a chance to occur, such as Killing Blow or Luck. When these skills work, you will see floating text letting you know. 

When a skill works and when you gain Skill XP, the floating text is blue. When gaining a level, the text is purple.

Skill Points are gained from completing quests, placing buildings, and killing monsters. There is no skill tree with prerequisites, so you can pick and choose whatever skills you want. There is also no maximum skill points that you can earn. I might add that later once I add more skills however. 

Please let me know what you think about the Skill XP gain rate as I am likely going to do a balance pass on it and your feedback would be a great help!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/f19400faed52cb4da792e59fe67b83a6e0340bb4.jpg[/img]

The current skills in this build are:
[list][*]Second Wind - when your hit points are reduced to 0, there is a chance that your health will partially regenerate, keeping you alive in the fight.
[*]Block Hit - when successfully blocking an attack you have a chance deal damage back to your opponent.
[*]Athletic - use less stamina when sprinting.
[*]Hard Head - dash attacks do additional damage. Stacks with the Ram Helmet.
[*]Killing Blow - when killing a monster with your power attack, there is a chance your power attack will immediately recharge.
[*]Tough Skin - reduces melee damage taken in combat.
[*]Spell Resist - reduces damage from spells.
[*]Luck - chance to increase the amount of loot (such as alchemy ingredients and ore) you get from treasure chests.
[*]Riches - chance to find more gold in treasure chests.[/list]

Placing a Barracks will allow you to assign the "Trainer" job to a townsperson. The Trainer gives you a bonus to your Skill Points earned and can be used to reset your spent skill points if you want to change where you spent them. This will obviously be more useful once there is a skill point cap.

This build also includes a bunch of improvements and some bug fixes.
[list][*]Quality Wood and Quality Stone now stack in your inventory.
[*]The same floating numbers that are used for the Skill System now also work when you take damage. They should be much easier to see now. Damage numbers appear in red.
[*]The Barracks are now cheaper to place (less gold) and only require a Carpenter and Stonemason rather than needing the Weaponsmith and Armorsmith Shops.
[*]You can now press and hold the Left Mouse Button to continue to attack. While holing the mouse button down, you can perform a power attack, block, or roll. Once that action is completed, your character will start using normal attacks again.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the spellcasters to cast a spell after they died.
[*]Fixed the Close button in the in-game settings UI.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the New Ore Discovered quest to not be given when it should be.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Alchemists to go to their home rather than their shop.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Shaydee to not accept the Quality Wood that you bring him to help build his shop.[/list]

notes.title: Coming Soon - Skill System
notes.content:
I've started work on the Skill System that I mentioned in the Roadmap update a few days ago and wanted to share some information.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/e57de31b6254a6cb64b461f53e0d4f87147a21e2.png[/img]

As you play the game your character will gain Skill Points. These points can be spent to obtain and upgrade skills. Each skill can be upgraded twice, creating three tiers for each skill counting the initial purchase.

Upgrading a skill will increase its chance to take effect and its potency. So for example, when initially purchased, "Tough Skin" reduces damage by 10%. Upgrading it will increase that 10% to 15% and upgrading it again increases it to 20%. I'm still working on the exact numbers, so take that as just an example.

Skill Points are gained from completing quests, completing construction of buildings, and killing monsters. I'm also considering giving a small increase to skill points earned if your overall town happiness is at 4 stars or above. I'm also still working out what the maximum number of skill points earned will be. Basically whether you can max out every skill eventually or limit it so you have to choose which ones to learn and upgrade and which ones to forgo.

There is no skill tree with prerequisites, so you can pick and choose whatever skills you want.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7a7d33bf3674811417cd9b0175b53dccb0725a8c.png[/img]
[list][*]Second Wind - when your hit points are reduced to 0, there is a chance that your health will partially regenerate, keeping you alive in the fight.
[*]Block Stun - when successfully blocking an attack you have a chance to stun your opponent.
[*]Athletic - use less stamina when sprinting.
[*]Hard Head - dash attacks do additional damage. Stacks with the Ram Helmet.
[*]Killing Blow - when killing a monster with your power attack, there is a chance your power attack will immediately recharge.
[*]Tough Skin - reduces melee damage taken in combat.
[*]Spell Resist - reduces damage from spells.
[*]Luck - chance to increase the amount of loot (such as alchemy ingredients and ore) you get from treasure chests.
[*]Riches - chance to find more gold in treasure chests.
[*]Nimble - reduce the amount of time to get back up when you are knocked down.
[/list]
I'm sticking to passive buffs and bonuses over activated skills for now. And of course I'm open to skill ideas! 

Also, the weapon and shield concepts are coming along nicely. So a sneak peek - The Copper Weapons! In addition to being the reference for the 3D models, I'm also going to use these as the icons in inventory and will eventually update all of the icons to match this style.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/fdaae01d3561fc2d362e9d4da37a7da397c98d6e.png[/img]
The concepts are being created by the same artist who drew the monsters. Really love his work!

And if you haven't checked out the roadmap yet, you can find it here:
https://steamcommunity.com/games/664000/announcements/detail/1710706508279875941

notes.title: Alpha 9.1 - Quick Fixes
notes.content:
A couple of quick, but important, bug fixes in tonight's build.

Fixed a bug that caused the "days" to fail to advance as time passed in the game. This was also affecting coal since if the day was never increasing, the coal system was never kicking in. It will start to work properly once four days have past since this fix.

I redid the system that tracks what ore you are eligible to unlock. The old system was prone to errors, such as sometimes not giving you the quest to upgrade ore or giving it to you, but then not increasing the ore after you completed the quest. So I did a quick re-write and it is much more stable now.[/list]

Also making some good progress on the skills system and have about 10 skills planned so far. Focusing on passive buffs and specials rather than stuff that would require lots of F-keys. The system is more about tailoring your character a bit without becoming overwhelming. 

When I say "buffs" though don't take that as just number increases. Some have special effects, such as the "Second Wind" skill that gives you a chance to not die when reduced to zero hit points and the "Killing Blow" skill which has a chance to immediately recharge your power attack if you kill a monster using a power attack.

I'll post an update about the skill system soon.

notes.title: Alpha 9.0 - Orc Quest Updates and Changes
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/968300d53d4bd89ef14cc1ae16ef5812ea66cfe5.jpg[/img]

Been getting some great feedback on the Orc Quest and spent some time working on a bunch of changes, improvements, and fixes. The quest is probably too long and feels too grindy, so a lot of the changes here attempt to address that. I might make some more changes later as well.

Note, if you have already started the Orc Quest on a save, then some of these changes may not apply. I'll separate the ones that apply to new quests vs. new and in-progress quests.

Applies to both new and in-progress quests
[list][*]Number of hits to chop down Desert Trees reduced from 7 down to 4.
[*]Number of hits to break Sandstone reduced from 6 down to 4.
[*]Reduced the amount of Desert Logs and Sandstone needed to make Orc Structures.
[*]Increased the yield from Sandstone from 1 to 2.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Shaman Hut to cost 0 Obsidian.
[*]Reduced the amount of Stamina that is lost when sprinting as an Orc.
[*]Added Orc Poles on the map to make finding the Orc Town a bit easier.
[*]Removed parts of the canyon to allow faster access to some areas of the map. You no longer have to run up and around the canyon as much.
[*]Skeletons move a bit faster.
[*]Reduced the time between each wave of Skeleton spawns in the final battle.
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused Obsidian Elementals to remain frozen in place after they are destroyed.
[/list]
These changes ONLY apply to saves that have NOT started the Orc Quest yet. Attempting to retrofit these into an already started quest chain would be too risky.
[list][*]Reduced the Obsidian cost for Orc structures.
[*]Removed the third Obsidian Quest since you no longer need as much.
[*]Moved the Orc Quest so that it starts later in the game. It was appearing too early, before you had a chance to really establish the town.
[/list]
This build also includes some other fixes.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the build sound to not play when helping Shaydee build his shop.
[*]When swapping NPC jobs with a shopkeeper, the new showkeeper will now correctly have wares to craft.
[*]Pressing ESC while moving a non-building structure such as a Water Well or Stone Fountain will no longer delete that structure. Pressing ESC when moving an existing structure shouldn't do anything since you can just put it back where it was. It's only used to cancel the placement of a new structure.
[*]Updated the method that monster spawners use to create loot. This is actually a pretty big change to some really old code and fixes a variety of race conditions that could occur resulting in loot failing to spawn.[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 8.10 - Sunray Update and More
notes.content:
Quick update today to go back to the old sun rays. I liked these more than the current one as they are more stylized and less obtrusive.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/1e9ef7eef14401df3f61ff7ca1dc14352103e52f.gif[/img]

This build also includes:
[list][*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the townsperson who is supposed to meet you during the Orc Quest to not appear.
[*]Some UI fixes including the credits screen and the welcome screen.
[*]Made some adjustments to lighting.
[*]Update to the Play Screen to get it to scale properly on widescreen monitors.
[/list]
Regarding the widescreen UI, right now I'm testing the Play Screen UI to make sure it scales properly for anyone using a widescreen resolution. To make sure we're on the same page, the Play Screen is the main UI with the PLAY button and other options.

I made some changes today that I think will do the trick. If it works, I'll need to update all of the UI to get those to all work. This will be a big undertaking, so I'll do it in phases as I work on other stuff.

This is what you should see if you try out Widescreen. Top image is 16:9 ratio and bottom is 32:9.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/c32552e6e035a34a7497f45dc45f1ef682740004.jpg[/img]

For now, if you'd like to try out a widescreen resolution you can use these cheat keys when the setting menu is open. While the menu is open, press and hold down left-shift and then:

Press 1 for 3840 x 1440
Press 2 for 2560 x 1080
Press 3 for 3840 x 1600
Press 4 for 3840 x 1080

You can also press 0 while holding down left-shift to reset back to 1920x1080.

[h1]Note to be clear, the rest of the rest of the game's UI *will not* look good yet in widescreen resolutions. I'm only testing the Play Screen itself. The windows that open from the Play Screen, like character selection, character creation, and settings are not updated yet.[/h1]

Once it is officially supported I'll put the options in the dropdown menu in Settings.

If everything looks good (or if it doesn't!) on the Play Screen, please feel free to post in this thread and let me know.

https://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/0/1729828401705901484/

notes.content:
Today's build includes some fixes and tweaks to monster spellcasters in addition to a couple of other fixes.
[list][*]Added a delay to the Orc Spellcaster's fireball attack so that the fireball was timed better with the Orc's animation.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused spellcaster healthbars to fail to blink before they cast a spell.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Goblin Spellcasters to leave their lightning attack on indefinitely.

notes.title: The Future of HammerHelm
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9dc2bad32061c792b24af6281adaa45747e3b216.jpg[/img]

It’s been a while since I talked about the longer-term plans for HammerHelm, and more specifically, the road to full release so I thought I’d do that today. Fair warning, this will probably be a long announcement!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/fc769fb078ad665a8eb7b1dec476baecd948a326.png[/img]

Before I start talking about the plans for HammerHelm I should probably begin with some background information. For the vast majority of HammerHelm’s development, both before and after launch (and right now) I’ve also worked a full time job. So all of the updates are developed outside of my normal work day, during the evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Those of you who have been with me for any length of time know that I update HammerHelm a lot! I always have time for HammerHelm and always will. I love working on this game and I love releasing new stuff for you all to enjoy. This isn't a "hobby project" for me...it's much, much bigger than that. While I do work with some super talented contract artists, I'm the only developer on HammerHelm. I also make all of the videos, screenshots, and gifs that you see supporting the updates. I do a lot ... and I love it!

The main reason I mention all of this is that I do work a full a time job and that’s why you rarely see me responding or updating the game during most weekdays during the day. Maybe someday HammerHelm will grow beyond my wildest expectations and I could work on it full-time, but for now that’s not the case and that's perfectly ok. Please rest assured that if you do post a comment or question or if you email me, I will respond.

When I first launched HammerHelm back in the summer of 2017, nearly every asset in the game was placeholder. HammerHelm was a bit rough around the edges admittedly, but over time new art, more content, and new features have been added. I look back at the game when it first launched and I barely recognize it.

I’m very happy with the direction HammerHelm is headed. And I must admit it’s not quite the direction I expected to go when I first launched. Your feedback and ideas have shaped HammerHelm in ways that I could never have anticipated and I am very grateful for that. It makes working on HammerHelm even more fun!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/ef5d85e3d83c4e7f56f08bf34ffc39750ca80038.png[/img]

So, how do we get HammerHelm out of Early Access? I’m glad you asked, because I have a plan and it breaks down to something like this:
[list][*]Replace the remaining placeholder monsters.
[*]Replace the major world assets (trees).
[*]Replace the armor and weapons.
[*]Add some more features and content – this is probably the biggest of the bunch here.
[*]Fix more bugs and continue to optimize and polish existing features.[/list]
Let me expand on the first four as the fifth one is pretty self-explanatory.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/ad7aefb1cb92b6903eb9b189b7119fb1813def5a.png[/img]

About half of the monsters have been updated in the game already and the remaining have concept art. The 3D artist who made the in-game assets for the new monsters is going to start on the last batch in about a month. This will likely take a few months to complete.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/e05f3493855db716353a2fb001da5c9cae58d0f7.png[/img]

Trees and other large flora will have a consistent art style that matches the rest of HammerHelm and will be better optimized. The work on this has just started. We’re going to focus on replacing the big trees first and then explore smaller things like bushes, flowers, and grass. Also, maybe some new textures for the ground, especially the town pathway.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/210d1cd5ca2a2b43ace549a071c940cbb8a4828d.png[/img]

Even though the characters got updated, the armor and weapons that you use are still the old art and don’t quite match. I’d like to replace those with new models in addition to having some kind of visual progression. So, a Blood Stone Hammer looks cooler than a Copper Hammer and not just a different color. This hasn’t started yet. It will be a pretty big undertaking and would likely start after the monsters are completed.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/fe149e82a0fa43e26919a3d164abdb9070b8d77f.png[/img]

Most of the core features of HammerHelm are in the game. Creating a character, building a town, all of the townspeople traits and jobs, quests and events, the main buildings, combat, monster AI, etc. I like the core gameplay so I want to focus on adding features that support and improve it. Some of this could be added during Early Access and some might be added after full release. In no particular order…
[list][*][b]Character skills.[/b] These are special abilities that allow you to define your character a bit more. Abilities can include everything from “tough skin” that makes you take less damage to really powerful things like if you kill a monster using your power attack there is a chance that your power attack will immediately recharge and you can use it again! Note, I don’t want to go too crazy with this as HammerHelm is more of an adventure game than a traditional RPG, but I think having a progression system for your character makes a lot of sense in a game like this. I’d likely add about 10 – 12 of these skills in addition to some kind of an XP system that would allow you to gain and improve the skills.
[*][b]Add some more life to the town.[/b] This is mostly having the townspeople move around their shops, do work, visit the tavern, etc. They won’t go to sleep (unless they are sick, see below) however as I’ve always found it annoying in games where you can’t speed up time to have to wait for an NPC to wake up.
[*][b]Add more meaningful events[/b] for the townspeople. When a townsperson falls ill, they actually go to bed. When hurt, they visit the infirmary (if there is one) or go home, eating binges at the tavern, and maybe brawls too.
[*][b]Alerts[/b] for when your town is low on a resource and other important messaging. This would be a full messaging system that could be used for various notes that you need to be aware of.
[*][b]Add a few more points of interest to the map.[/b]
[*][b]Add some more uses for alchemy ingredients other than potions.[/b]
[*][b]Controller support.[/b]
[*][b]Add some kind of fast travel system[/b] especially once I fill in the remainder of the map and you are sent further away from your town.
[*][b]More customization.[/b] A few more hair and beard styles. Skin tones too.
[*][b]Add some more Steam Achievements.[/b]
[*][b]Add some more items to place in your home.[/b]
[*][b]More quests.[/b]
[*][b]Other stuff not mentioned here[/b] because I haven’t thought of it yet![/list]
That’s of course not a full list, but it’s where my thoughts are for now and feels like a solid direction.

One more thing I want to say about full release is that when HammerHelm leaves Early Access nothing really changes for me. I’m still going to update the game and I’m still going to add new features, more content, add new and improved art, and fix bugs. It’s really more of a signal that the game’s core features and gameplay are in a state that I am happy with and that you all are happy with too!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/874cf211601da511dd6bff00077d3cf8bc7161df.png[/img]

Now on to something else. Mod support and multi-player. I get asked about those two features a lot and I’ve talked about them at various times in updates and forum posts, so I’ll pretty much say what I’ve always said. 

They’re both unlikely, certainly not before leaving Early Access. For multi-player, it just wasn’t something I ever considered for HammerHelm. Many of the game’s core systems wouldn’t really support multiple characters anyway. So “unlikely” probably isn’t a strong enough word, it’s almost definitely not in the cards.

With mod support, that’s something I’m not closing the door on, but I also want to be clear that in HammerHelm’s case it’s much easier said than done. It’s something I’m investigating but for now let’s assume it’s not part of the plan. I’m exploring using an extension that would allow mods to be created in Unity (the engine I use to create HammerHelm), but that needs some more investigation. So, I say “unlikely” mostly because I’ve done only a very small amount of research into it and I never want to promise something and then not deliver on it. That would stink.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/05d2339e6fc865f5f275da9401cfe3a76aa26da6.png[/img]

One more thing I wanted to talk about (and it’s a big one!) is Survival/Sandbox Mode. I’ve had a lot of people ask me about creating a mode in HammerHelm that has more survival and sandbox elements in it and while I haven’t started any meaningful work on the idea and it’s not on the above roadmap, I want to talk about it because I think it could be cool. 

I’ve thought about this a bit and I don’t think simply adding survival elements to the current game would make sense or be fun. I can’t imagine trying to actually track the hunger of almost 50 characters in a large town, having them die off because of the cold, while also having to complete the quests that keep popping up, let alone the other complexities in the current game! 

But I do think there is an opportunity to do something unique and fun with HammerHelm. When I think about this, I think about it as a new mode within HammerHelm. I think of something smaller, yet larger. What I mean by that is a smaller town but a larger world. A mode where you take on more of the resource gathering, crafting, and building responsibilities, but still have a village and some townspeople that you are growing and nurturing. 

It’s more of a sandbox, with less focus on quests and more focus on exploration. Monsters, Caves, Dungeons, and other obstacles would be scattered across the map, and always be there for you to find on your own. So, it’s less about the game giving you challenges and more about finding your own! It’s not about tracking food and water meters though, but rather, its more personal, focusing on your character and exploration, but still maintaining some town gameplay that sets it apart and makes it feel “HammerHelm”. I think it could be a really fun way to play HammerHelm without forcing big changes to the core game that all you initially came here to play.

Maybe a crazy idea. Maybe something I shouldn’t even talk about yet. But I like to provide you with some insight into my longer term thinking and get your feedback. I’d rather throw it out there than keep it myself since if you all hate the idea, then the last thing I’d want to do is spend months and months working on it only to be booed off of Steam! :) And if you are intrigued by the idea (and I hope you are because I think it would be really cool!) then I’ll spend some more time experimenting with designs in the background while continuing to release the main updates I talked about above.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/95b69ed40fe88250fef3692ef737622f3d4b48a4.png[/img]

Lastly, I want to close by expanding on something I wrote on my Twitter account the other day that I think is fitting since we’re talking about what’s next for HammerHelm. 

Apparently, there are over 30,000 games on Steam now. Thirty thousand! It is incredibly humbling to know that from all of those choices, you all found HammerHelm and decided to support it. I have been in the games industry for over 20 years now and making this game has been a life long dream of mine. And it wouldn't mean anything without all of you. All I can say is thank you and hope you're as excited about the future of HammerHelm as I am!

As always if you have any questions, concerns, or feedback feel free to write me a note! I’ve created a forum thread so we can discuss things together and/or you're more than welcome to email me directly.

https://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/0/1744483505471025947/

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
Founder and Developer, SuperSixStudios
- [i]supersixstudios@gmail.com[/i]
- [i]https://twitter.com/SuperSixStudios[/i]

notes.title: Alpha 8.7 - Warmth System
notes.content:
Today's build has the Warmth System and some physics for the Ratmen and Mushroom-men. The Warmth System is the final "house effects" system, joining the Water, Beauty, and Cleanliness systems.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/af2405273e2d4646611f6a475a0962315b17b115.png[/img]

The warmth system uses coal to heat houses that have fireplaces built. If a house doesn't have a fireplace or the town does not have any coal, then the house will not be heated that evening. A cold house causes a minor mood debuff while a warm house provides a positive buff. I have the mood debuff set really low as this system will likely need some balance tweaks. 

The system doesn't start checking for fireplaces and coal until the fifth day to give you time. Also, when a fireplace is first placed it is pre-lit, providing warmth until the sun sets and the coal is needed again. This means if you have a home that gets a fireplace built before the fifth day, you actually get the benefit until the sun sets on the fifth day.

A wooden house needs two coal per day for its fireplace whereas a stone house only needs one. The warmth system only uses coal for now. It might use wood at some point, but I've found that automatically using wood makes building new structures tricky.

The warmth overlay displays a flame icon in the upper right. In this case, it shows that two of the houses have heat. The rest do not.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/0b046961f5ab4bda2a4a788cd4b95b138942463c.jpg[/img]

When a house has coal, its chimney emits smoke and the fireplace has a fire in it. In this case, the town ran out of coal, so Tery's house doesn't have smoke coming from its chimney. His neighbor got the last pieces of coal, so that house's chimney shows the smoke. If you went inside that house, you'd see fire in the fireplace, whereas Tery's fireplace wouldn't be lit. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/403a84f1de31e8251536b81ef6a516c6e29aea93.jpg[/img]


[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/5a34f389b343ab3023055a77255f1ac25b88d79a.png[/img]

The Ratman's tail and ears now have physics as does the Mushroom-man's tongue.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/114e78d1bb4165adf3fb85f5fdfd2decaa1c19a6.gif[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/976041d82f8928939acc8d01e60bf4f6cf0b13ca.gif[/img]

This build also a few fixes and changes.
[list][*]Fixed a bug fix that caused building lights to not turn on when loading a save at night.
[*]Increased the amount of Coal a Miner can carry from two to four.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Miners to leave the mine quicker than intended.

notes.title: Alpha 8.2 - Bug Fixes and Tweaks
notes.content:
I mentioned in an earlier announcement that I wanted to spend some time shoring up HammerHelm and making it more stable. I'll get back to adding new stuff soon, but I think with the speed that I was adding new content, I feel behind a bit on polish and bugs. So today's build is another round of bug fixes and some tweaks to improve movement and combat.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/a3f6e8e77ba07f115e90fe8385da26951eb0d5bb.png[/img]
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused buildings with open doors to sometimes block the character from entering. 
[list][*]This was a big one and I actually rewrote the door code to get it working correctly.
[*]Because both the player character and townspeople (Carpenters) can open building doors and since HammerHelm doesn't zone you into an interior like many other games do, there is a lot to account for with doors!
[*]The bug was due to a safety check where I didn't let the player go through a door that was in the middle of it's closing animation. The game would essentially create an invisible barrier. This is because while nobody is in a house, the interior is actually turned off to improve performance. So in the old system, without that safety check, you'd walk into a house with a grass floor and nothing in it! 
[*]The bug was caused by the door thinking it was closing, but never actually finishing its close animation, and hence not removing the invisible barrier. 
[*]The new method no longer needs this check and overall is a lot cleaner. If you do notice any other strange behavior with doors please do let me know.[/list]
[*]Fixed some areas of the cave that weren't lined up correctly.
[*]Fixed a bug that spawned Fire and Ice Elementals when the spawner should have been making Earth and Stone Elementals.
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused monsters to stop attacking after the first one in the group was killed. They were just in awe of your fighting skills! :P
[*]Fixed some bugs that caused the power-attack gems to get out of sync with whether you could do a power attack or not.
[*]Tweaked some of the numbers in combat, specifically attack ranges and knockback amounts, to reduce the issue of clipping into monsters while fighting them. This was especially noticeable with Elementals and other large monsters.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused you to lose your power attack if you missed an attack.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Stone and Earth Elementals to jump on your head when trying to attack causing them to never get in attack range (funny, but not exactly a good tactic on their part!)
[*]Adjusted some times with regards to rolling to stop the character's movement when the roll finished. When these times were off a little, the character would slide a bit after a roll.[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7d55d00d137d25e1eb80e5725f9d066b800fb63a.png[/img]

In addition to these fixes and tweaks I also added in some unofficial support for widescreen monitors. Note, I say "unofficial" because I don't own a widescreen so I can't test how they look with the UI. In fact, I know the UI gets messed up... 

But if you want to try it out and send me screenshots of any UI that doesn't look right, I might be able to fix them and then officially support that resolution. Also let me know which UI look good, so I can find commonalities between the good looking UI and the UI that needs to be updated.

To use a wide screen resolution open the Settings Menu. While the menu is open, press and hold down left-shift and then:

Press 1 for 3840 x 1440
Press 2 for 2560 x 1080
Press 3 for 3840 x 1600

You can also press 0 while holding down left-shift to reset back to 1920x1080.

If there are other resolutions you'd like me to support I can add them to this as well. If I get enough feedback and examples of a resolution or if it just looks great right away (most resolutions should scale properly) I can add it officially once we think the UI looks good at that resolution.

Feel free to email me at: supersixstudios@gmail.com with any UI (or anything else for that matter!)

notes.title: Alpha 8.0 - Sound Settings and Tavern Work
notes.content:
Happy New Year everyone!

Today's update includes a much needed and long awaited feature - separate sliders for Music and Sound settings! Adding this actually required a fairly large change to the way sound works in the game but I think HammerHelm has been around far too long without them.

You can adjust the settings in either the title menu or when in game after pressing ESC.

Also regarding sounds, once you've had a chance to play with the settings, if there are any sounds that are too loud or too quiet compared to others let me know. I'm doing a volume pass on the sounds and music to set them closer together.

This build also includes the Tavern Cellar. You can enter the cellar by using the door at the back inside of the tavern. I'll be using this for some quests in future updates!

Speaking of the Tavern, I'm also updating it. Right now, the second story floor and the main roof are really low, causing the game to look like this when the camera shifts down under the ceiling:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/3d2d4423dd4f3d7dfd21430ad519a1ebdf421257.jpg[/img]

Ew.

The new Tavern is going to be raised a bit. I didn't want to add two more stories as that would make the Tavern far too large. So I added a row of vertical wood between the first and second floor and another between the second floor and the roof. It not only raises the building but it also creates what I think is a nice break in the look of the Tavern's normal stone and wood walls.

Work in progress shot:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/8163e08f2d547c47dded14e745b988479fccb00d.gif[/img]

The net effect of this is a much nicer looking screen when you are inside the tavern (again, still WIP, but I'm pretty happy with the result)
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/fda5057ed685378a1865d68a5270fb7cca6523c1.jpg[/img]

You can also see the cellar door in front of my character.

A couple of other things in this build:
[list][*]Fixed a bug that caused the diagonal running animation to persist after releasing the A or D keys and continuing to run forward.
[*]Turned off the Holiday lights and Santa Hats (booooo!)[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 7.4: Mushroom-men and Skeletons
notes.content:
Another day, another build! Really having fun with the new monsters and I hope you are enjoying them too! Today's build has new monster attacks for the Skeletons and Mushroom-men and a new death effect for the Skeletons!

[h1][b]New Skeleton Death Effects[/b][/h1]
When killing a skeleton they drop their weapons to the ground and burn away. It might be a bit tricky to see in the gif but I tried to center the dead skeleton so you can see the effect and the weapons dropping clearly.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/77a62322a95a1c14d7c04f8793de234d4fff13db.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Skeleton Brute Sweep Attack[/b][/h1]
Skeleton Brutes carry two-handed halberds and can perform a leg sweep attack that will knock you over. This is similar to the Orc Brute's smash attack, except it knocks you down in place rather than knocking you back. In some ways, this is MORE dangerous because the monsters are closer to you and may get in a free hit! Before performing a leg sweep attack a blood-like effect will appear on their weapon as well as near their healthbar.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/50995b4b028c25bf63abed22e31fc529b6495b29.gif[/img]

Like all special attacks, they cannot be blocked. But dodging or running away works just fine.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7171061df2c9a7da2802bc36ca2d5d9ddcfba384.gif[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/a600ca88728c03174d58a4993093b0c418bea085.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Mushroom-man Spellcaster[/b][/h1]
And last, but never least, our friend the Mushroom-man. Still can't tell if he's actually casting a spell or ate some bad oysters. Either way, best to roll out of the way! Mushroom-men Spellcasters are purple with white caps and do not carry a club or shield.
