notes.title: Alpha 7.0: Monster AI and Combat Update
notes.content:
Today's build includes the new monster AI, updated combat (power attack and rolling), monster types (Grunts, Brutes, and Spellcasters) as well as some other fixes and optimizations. Not all of the monsters have a spellcaster and a brute yet. I wanted to release this and get your feedback before adding more.

Updated Trailer:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Grj63iFMKHA
This update includes three new monsters models - the new Mushroom-man, the new Goblin, and the Ratman in addition to the new Skeleton and new Orc that were added a while back!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/28ff0a92de2c0c0765f036f551c98f9edb3f6548.png[/img]Monsters will have two or three different types that can be encountered.
[list][*]Regular versions of monsters (called "Grunts") attack as normal. Health bar blinks, the run in if they aren't in melee range, and then attack. These attacks can be blocked. These monsters always have one weapon and sometimes a shield. Monster spawners always create at least one Grunt before deciding whether to create another type.
[*]More powerful versions of monsters (called "Brutes") attack as normal too, but also have special attacks that cannot be blocked and must be dodged.  Brutes will stand out from Grunts based on their weapons. This can be a large weapon (such as the Orc Brute's Hammer), dual wielding weapons, or other setups. When a Brute is about to perform a special attack they will yell and their healthbar will turn orange in addition to blinking.
[*]The final type of monster are Spellcasters. They can use a variety of spells for both attack and defense. Spellcasters are unarmed and sometimes may have some other visual cue so you can tell they are a spellcaster. Attack spells will generally have a "charge" and a "shot" so you'll have time to react to the spell before it is cast. Some spells, such as the Ratman's spell have an area of effect. Entering this area will cause you to take damage until you leave it or the spell expires. Hitting a spellcaster will not interrupt its spell.[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/cbdf4d61fac5ead77adfdb19cb6fa4697f979c6b.gif[/img]
[i]A Ratman Spellcaster will call magic vines from the ground to protect himself if you get too close.[/i]


[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/b46c09aad07a42ce4ad839f899262631937e543a.png[/img]Some monster types will have a Brute class. Brute doesn't mean that they are necessarily bigger or stronger, just that they are more elite and more dangerous.
[list][*]Orc Brutes - Wield a larger hammer, have additional hitpoints and can perform a smash attack. Smash attacks do additional damage and can knock you down.
[*]Goblin Brutes - Wield a two-handed sword and can perform a spin attack, dealing damage to you as the blade hits until you move out of the way..
[*]Ratman Brutes, Skeleton Brutes, and Mushroom-men Brutes are in development.[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/c466a3e45590ad64877935e79fe0d0987d9f2fc8.gif[/img]
[i]A Goblin Brute performs his deadly spin attack..[/i]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/ec3130bba78eee7a33c06730a21c29b5ebc879bc.png[/img]Some monsters have spellcasters that can cast various spells. Projectile spells cannot be blocked and therefor must be dodged.
[list][*]Goblin Spellcasters - can cast a lighting attack.
[*]Orc Spellcasters - focus on damage, can cast a fireball.
[*]Ratman Spellcasters - can cast a spell creating vines from the ground that will damage you if you are near them.
[*]Mushroom-Man and Skeleton Spellcasters as well as more spells for the existing spellcasters will be in a future update.
[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/e125bcf6735a358607946a367e0a4d4f6253d089.gif[/img]
[i]Just barely dodging a fireball attack from an Orc Spellcaster.[/i]

Other monsters such as the Elementals, Scarecrows, and Ghosts won't have Brutes or Spellcasters yet. I have a reason for that, that I'm not quite ready to reveal yet. :) 

The Necromancer's spell and damage invulnerability will remain the same. 

This update also includes additional tutorial screens explaining the new Brutes and Spellcasters. These appear in the tutorial Goblin Camp quest. I haven't added them to the ESC menu yet, but I plan to do so in a future update. You can check them out below:

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/8345739a4de44ba37b6f639652b657eeb5d1ef85.jpg[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/aae8ca7da74d8082bf48c22b8f6a364a737b2c52.jpg[/img]

Other changes in this update:
[list][*]Rolling is more reliable now as pressing a roll key will interrupt whatever your character is doing and immediately perform the roll.
[*]You don't take damage from normal melee attacks if you are rolling in addition to avoiding spells and special attacks.
[*]The Dash Attack no longer knocks monsters down. I'm debating what to do with this ability, but leaving it in since it's part of a quest.
[*]Sounds originating from something that isn't right next to you should be a bit louder now. This was important to change as the Brutes and Spellcasters make audio cues before attacking.
[*]Added the correct sounds to Orcs. Some were using the old sounds.
[*]Updated Shaydee to use the new Goblin model.
[*]Replaced the Ghosts in the storehouse in the tutorial quest with Ratmen.
[*]Temporarily turned off the Where's The Beer quest until I can figure out why the Kegs don't appear sometimes. If you have this quest now, you will still be able to complete it.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused you to get the Shaydee Business quest again even if you've already completed it.[/list]

[i]You made it all the way to the bottom? Congrats! Click this :)[/i]

notes.title: Monster Progress and AI Info
notes.content:
All five of the new monsters are set up and built for the new AI system I am working on so I wanted to share a group shot I took and give you an update!

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/263994be36709cab8426286fe068b1332fff43e4.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/263994be36709cab8426286fe068b1332fff43e4.jpg[/img][/url]
[i](click to see larger image)[/i]

First, I'm beyond happy with how these turned out, from the concept art to the 3D model and textures. I'm very lucky to have such skilled artists working on these for me.

We did find some errors in their rigs that need to be addressed so I can set them up with their new animations. For example, in the shot above you can see that the Ratman has his left foot way off the ground. That's his two-handed weapon idle pose, so his foot is supposed to be a lot closer to the ground. You can't see it, but his hands also don't line up quite right on the sword's handle.

For the new monster AI, I've decided to rewrite it so I can do more with it. Here's what I am currently working on. Note some of this may change as I work on it and test it out.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/28ff0a92de2c0c0765f036f551c98f9edb3f6548.png[/img]Monsters will have two or three different types that can be encountered.
[list][*]Regular versions of monsters (called "Grunts" in the code) attack as normal. Health bar blinks, the run in if they aren't in melee range, and then attack. These attacks can be blocked. These monsters always have one weapon and sometimes a shield. Monster spawners always create at least one Grunt before deciding whether to create another type.
[*]More powerful versions of monsters (called "Brutes" in the code) attack as normal too, but also have special attacks that cannot be blocked and must be dodged.  Brutes will stand out from Grunts based on their weapons. This can be a large two-handed weapon (like the Ratman in the image above), dual wielding weapons, or other setups. When a Brute is about to perform a special attack there will be a visual and audio cue to let you know in addition to the healthbar blink. I'm still working on this part.
[*]The final type of monster are Spellcasters. They can use a variety of spells for both attack and defense. Spellcasters are unarmed and sometimes may have some other visual cue so you can tell they are a spellcaster. Attack spells will generally have a "charge" and a "shot" so you'll have time to react to the spell before it is cast. Hitting a spellcaster will not interrupt its spell.[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/b46c09aad07a42ce4ad839f899262631937e543a.png[/img]Some monster types will have a Brute class. Brute doesn't mean that they are necessarily bigger or stronger, just that they are more elite and more dangerous.
[list][*]Orc Brutes - Wield a larger hammer, have additional hitpoints and can perform a smash attack. Smash attacks do additional damage and can knock you down.
[*]Goblin Brutes - Dual wield daggers and can perform a sneak attack causing a "disarm" adding a timer before you can attack again.
[*]Ratman Brutes - Wield two-handed swords with a special attack that adds a "bleed" effect to you, causing additional damage over time.
[*]Skeleton Brutes - Wield a two-handed weapon and will perform a special attack that will do something cool once I decide what it is. :)  [/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/ec3130bba78eee7a33c06730a21c29b5ebc879bc.png[/img]Some monsters have spellcasters that can cast various spells. Projectile spells cannot be blocked and therefor must be dodged.
[list][*]Goblin Spellcasters - can cast a direct damage attack, a shield spell, and a damage debuff.
[*]Orc Spellcasters - focus on damage, can cast a direct damage attack and a damage (strength) buff for other Orcs.
[*]Skeleton Spellcasters - can cast a direct damage attack and can sometimes summon another skeleton (this might be in a phase 2) 
[*]Ratman Spellcasters - can cast a poison attack that causes damage over time and a shield spell.
[*]Mushroom-Man Spellcasters - not really a spellcaster in the traditional sense, but can spit a stream of fire or other element that damages you the longer you stay in it.
[/list]
Shield spells must be damaged with attacks to bring them down so you can damage the monster again. They can be cast on the spellcaster and/or on its allies. This kind of works like a heal in some ways as it means the monster must take damage beyond its starting hitpoints to kill it. I'm avoiding traditional heals for now and using shields instead because of the way the monster health cubes work. They were never set up to be put back after a monster takes damage and they fall off.

Other monsters such as the Elementals, Scarecrows, and Ghosts won't have Brutes or Spellcasters yet. I want to focus on the new monsters first. My hope is to change out some of the remaining monsters and then add more to them too. The Necromancer's spells and damage invulnerability will remain the same. Golems will also keep their special attack (basically they are all Brutes) but will have the visual cue added similar to other Brutes.

As you can probably tell, all of this combined is a really big change, but I think it'll go a long way to making combat in HammerHelm much better. Right now I think combat is a bit of a weak link for HammerHelm so I want to put some real focus on it to make it a lot more fun and engaging.

notes.title: Alpha 6.2 - Improvements and Fixes
notes.content:
Today's build includes a couple of requested improvements to existing systems and a few bug fixes.
[list][*]You can now hold down left-shift and press the take or give arrow buttons in the Town Storage UI. Doing this will take all of a resource from the Storehouse up until your inventory is full or give all the resource you have in your inventory to the Storehouse up until the town's maximum depending on which button your press.
[*]Added a message above the quests to "Press TAB to cycle active quest" when you have two or more quests. A lot of new players have told me they didn't know you can TAB through the quests.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the maximum number of quests you can have to be five, rather than three, after completing the Orc Quest.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Cookhouse building to only display the roof rather than the entire building. This was a bug related to the optimizations I did. Not showing the building at all is one sure way to optimize it, but it doesn't look very nice. :)
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused a newly placed building to be ignored by the Workers.[/list]
And a quick shot of the MusroomMen wielding weapons and armor in a cave. I think I really like these guys having weapons and armor over having nothing. Will need to create some variety with them along with the kind that explodes. I might make that kind not carry weapons or armor so they stand out more. Hoping to get the final textures for the MushroomMen and Goblins and get them all in the game some time next week!

Today's build includes some fixes and improvements to the Orc Quest.

notes.title: Alpha 5.0: Orctober Test Build!
notes.content:
i just uploaded a test build for the Orctober Event. If you would like to help test the event, you can do so by doing the following:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - OrctoberTest - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game. You should see an image for the event on the title screen.


[h1][b]NOTE: This is a huge piece of content and I'm still testing, so I highly advise you make a backup of your save before loading into the Orc Event Test Build.[/b][/h1]


To start the Orc event, simply unlock Shaydee the Goblin (if you don't have him already) and clear out any quests you have. Once the system decides to start the event, it will stop giving you new quests so you can clear them out easily. The first quest is called "Trick or Treat". Once you get that quest, you should NOT get any additional quests except those related to the event.

To give you an idea of how big this is compared to other quests...most quests in HammerHelm have between 3 and 4 parts. The Orctober Quest is around 40 parts! Not to mention the new land, a (simple) town attack system, new monster models, new AI to support ranged attackers, and a bunch of other new things!

In fact, it's so big, I made a post-it chart to plan it out. This is what it looks like on my wall. :)

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/dbf895a4b8d48571285f1d9a83f354907769f3eb.jpg[/img]

A few things to note. A couple of the quests direct you to the same cave. I'm still working on adding a couple more caves to diversify those quests a bit more. 

If you finish the quest, one thing to look for is any oddities in your town after you get back to it. Especially with the NPCs. During the quest your town is essentially turned off, otherwise townspeople would go hungry and such while you were playing the event. Once you finish the event, everything should turn back on and go back to normal.

I'll be testing today and tomorrow as well so I will likely be creating a new test build tomorrow evening as well.

Please feel free to post any bugs or feedback in the forums:
https://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/1/1736594593611949688/

To get back to the live build:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

[h1]Any saves generated while testing the event should not be loaded if you go back to the regular client before the event is fully live.[/h1]

If all goes well, my plan is to launch the event for everyone on Tuesday as I would like a good day of testing on Monday. 

Apologies again for the delays, I may have bitten off a bit more than I should have chewed with this but I'm having fun making it and I hope you all find it fun too!

notes.title: Alpha 4.6.0 - Combat Tweaks and Fixes
notes.content:
Today's update includes some tweaks to combat, mostly related to animations. In the previous system, the attack animations always played the entire way through, meaning the animation would play and then return to the start position before playing the next animation. 

The new system blends the animations together better, so as long as you are clicking, the character will attack much more fluidly. 

Visually, it's a pretty big change and I think it feels much better this way. Please let me know what you think as I can tweak the timing as I get feedback.

This build also includes some more fixes:
[list][*]Removed the shininess from the some of the buildings. This was an artifact of the the roof hueing changes I made. You can see the difference in the screenshot below between the old (top) and new (bottom) look of the buildings.
[*]The mouse sensitivity slider in the options menu will no longer reset back to its default when opening the settings UI. You may have to go into the settings UI to reset the mouse sensitivity slider to your preference, but after doing that it will remain in the correct spot whenever you open the settings UI in the future.
[*]As part of the combat update, I also fixed the bug that sometimes caused the character to get stuck when blocking, forcing you to right-click again to clear it.[/list]

[b]Building material fix to remove the glossiness.[/b]

notes.title: Optimization Progress Update
notes.content:
I mentioned in an earlier announcement that I wanted to focus on optimization for a bit to help the game run better, especially on lower spec machines. I'm still working on stuff, but I wanted to share something that I hope you all will find pretty cool.

Right now every building in the game uses it's own material to determine what it looks like. For the most part this is because they have different roof colors and I've used a paint program to manually create each different color. Thing is, materials use up a lot of memory and a large town might have 15-20 materials, just for the buildings.

So I'm working on changing the way the materials work with the buildings. Without getting into too much of the technical stuff, the new method will allow buildings to share the same material, while also having different roof colors.

As a side-effect of this change, I can also add the ability for YOU to determine the roof colors and even allow for the same kind of building to have different colors.

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/bcaa16eff42ea19614c06a42e11e5ea348e9fda9.jpg][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/bcaa16eff42ea19614c06a42e11e5ea348e9fda9.jpg[/img][/url]

What you are looking at above is a test, using five wooden houses all with different roof colors. In the current system, this would be five materials, and be limited by the colors I chose when making them. In the new system, these are updated in code, while the game is running. So not only is it ONE material instead of five, but the color choices could be almost anything as well.

Want every building in your town to have a red roof? Done. How about a rainbow town? Sure! You get the idea. :)

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/2402fe2f0d3fed8a09f79760880cb3f2c6ea3b06.gif[/img]

Reducing the materials will save a lot on memory and since doing the optimization could also unlock more customization, it's a no-brainer!. It's going to take me a bit of time to update all of the buildings to use this new method (and then also add a way for you to change the colors), but I think it'll be worth it.

notes.title: Alpha 3.3.0 - Quest Manager Update and More
notes.content:
Today's build includes a really big update to the Quest Manager. Most of this is behind the scenes, but it's a much better system that allows for more control over quests. 

In this new system you should never go really long periods of time without having a quest and you won't get a new quest immediately after finishing one. The system also adjusts when new quests are created based on how many quests you have active.

This update also includes:
[list][*]Workers who are set to gather stone will continue to do so when the Trees are cursed.
[*]Carpenters and Stonemasons now go back to the shops rather than going home when they cannot craft furniture or fireplaces.
[*]Carpenters and Stonemasons who aren't working will tell you that they don't have enough resources if you click the About button when speaking with them.
[*]The grass distance slider works for all terrains, rather than just the one your town is in.
[*]The item quantity in Inventory will no longer display when there is no item in that slot.
[*]Removed the yell and arm wave "wind up" from Mushroommen prior to attacking. This was causing confusion as to when to block after a Mushroomman's health bar blinked. They now attack as soon as the bar stops blinking.
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused a townsperson to not start mining right away after being assigned as a Miner.
[*]Fixed the location of a stone that was inside a tree, making it impossible for Workers to get to it.
[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 3.2.2 - Harvesting, Food, and Cooking
notes.content:
Today's update includes some changes to the overall food system in the game. Most of this is intended to ease the difficulty of keeping your townspeople well fed, especially in the early stages of a town. 

After looking into the numbers more, the amount of raw food being produced was lower than I wanted and that of course could create food shortages if Cooks didn't have enough raw materials to prepare enough meals for the town.

The changes include:
[list][*]Increased Farm production for raw vegetables by 33% per plot.
[*]Increased the amount of raw meat Hunters obtain by 40%.
[*]Increased the maximum amount of meals Cooks can produce by 10%.
[*]Increased the benefit of the "Foodie" trait by 10%. This stacks with the Cook increase.
[*]Townspeople now eat once a day, in the evening.[/list]

Note that last change means for existing saves, you might have townspeople get the "I didn't eat today" debuff the first time they eat since they are all eating their food in one sitting. But assuming you are making enough food, it should clear up by the next evening.

Thank you every for your feedback!

Note there are some rules related to job swapping to be aware of:
[list][*]You cannot swap jobs with a Townsperson who has a quest. notes.title: Quick Roadmap Update - Job Swapping
notes.content:
I wanted to give some quick information about what I'm focusing on next in the immediate future.

Ability to change townspeople jobs. This is the big one that is the most requested feature. You will be able to swap townspeople jobs. So if you get a new Dwarf who has the Green Thumb trait and want to make him a farmer, but already have someone assigned to be a Farmer, you'll be able to give him that job and the former Farmer will go back to being a Worker who can then be assigned to a different job. 

Originally HammerHelm Dwarves didn't have traits so it didn't matter which Dwarf got which job. But now that they do, this feature is a must. This is a fairly complicated feature however as it has to account for all sorts of edge cases but I'm actively working on it as I know it is an important and necessary addition.

I also want to add some more quality of life improvements, including more pop-up information. Mousing over the resources in the main UI when in your town will tell you what the resource name is and possibly some more information. I'm also going to add pop-up information to the buildings when in build mode to give you more info about the building and the Dwarves that live or work there.

And of course, more quests. I'm probably going to finish the top two items before adding a bunch more quests, but I definitely want to add more Story Quests in addition to more variety of normal quests.

notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/6562eeec754bc3380f2c6bc7502813d78828a3fc.gif[/img]

Today's build includes a change to combat that makess it feel more responsive, especially when using the power-attack or trying to block after attacking. 

In the old system, if you were clicking to attack and then pressed block while the attack animation was playing, the block wouldn't always register. The same was true if you tried to use a Power-Attack too early.

Now it not only do they work, but in the case of blocking, you can also block much earlier than before and your character will transition to block much faster. Note that clicking to attack and then immediately blocking can interrupt your attack. This change should also remove long delays between attacks that sometimes could occur.

Hopefully you can see the speed at which the block transitions in the gif below. Would love to hear what everyone thinks once you've had a chance to try it. It's not a *huge* change, but it should feel better.

This update also includes:

notes.title: Big Terrain Optimization Test Build
notes.content:
I just finished a really big optimization pass on the terrain and I've released it as a test build. I've tested it a LOT myself, but it's a really big change, so I could use some help testing it.

The terrain in the live build (2.5.0) is one big object. Every time it needs to be updated (such as when you place a structure) it requires a lot of memory. The new terrain is split into nine pieces, so when you place a structure, only the piece of terrain where your town is gets updated. For anyone who has experienced a crash when placing a structure, this optimization should resolve that.

Doing this also has some other benefits. You may have also noticed that after placing a building there is a small delay (about 1 second) before the Build Menu reappears. Because of this optimization, the delay has gone down from 1 second to 0.0024 seconds! You might also notice the game playing a bit smoother depending on where you are in the world.

All of this is behind the scenes so when you load your game with the new terrain, you shouldn't notice any difference at all.

If you'd like to help test the new Terrain you can do so by following these instructions. Before loading your save with this test build, make a backup just in case. I've run a number of saves and everything seems good, but always better to be safe. :)

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - HammerHelmTest - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game.

[h1]Note that once you load this new build, you won't be able to load that save with the Alpha client, so again, good idea to make a backup of your save.[/h1]

[b]Stuff to look for are things that spawn in the world, such as monsters, ore deposits, the Dreadbloom, treasure chests, dungeon/cave entrances, and anything that spawns in your town such as the scarecrows, cursed farm fog, treasure chests from townspeople, etc.[/b]


If everything looks good you can continue to play using the test build. I'm planning on releasing it tomorrow (July 2) if all goes well. After that your new saves will work with the Live build.

But if you want to get back to the Alpha client before that, just follow these instructions:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

Thanks in advance everyone! I know on the surface this won't look like much, but it's a really big change for the better that I am super happy with so far. :)

notes.title: Test Build 1.7: Big Balance Update and Fixes
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7fc86da859f5018f3031f432e5ff537b6b45f41f.png[/img]

Today's build has a really big update to game balance, including the costs and pre-requisites for buildings, townspeople resource gathering, and townspeople resource use. I feel like this is getting pretty close to where I want it to be and I'm hoping to go live with the Big Update for everyone before next weekend!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/1684d275fd2dee00536cdbdc214a27aa26fab72a.png[/img]
The biggest change here is the increase in Storehouses from 2 to 3 and a reduction to Ore and Alchemy storage. I'm trying to find a good balance between the townspeople gathering resources for you vs. you getting resources from questing and other methods. 64 was what I wanted the maximum to be for 4 Storehouses (my original designed limit although I never implemented it) so leaving it at 64 per Storehouse would have meant a 192 maximum, which is crazy high. 
[list][*]Increased storehouse limit from 2 to 3
[*]Storehouse maximum capacity changes:
[list][*]Quality Wood and Quality Stone changed from 64 to 40 (note there are lots of building resource requirement reductions so this isn't a bad thing!)
[*]Food changed from 170 to 165.
[*]Ore reduced from 64 to 25.
[*]Alchemy Ingredients reduced from 64 to 25.
[*]Raw Meat and Raw Veggies reduced from 170 to 165[/list][/list]
Keep in mind, that you CAN take resources from the Storehouses, so effectively the cap isn't a huge deal if you take from the Storehouse. And with 3 Storehouses the total cap is 75 - which I honestly think is still too high, but for now I'll stick with it. I just didn't want the town stockpiling so many Ore and Alchemy that the rest of the game became irreverent. Also right now, the town uses a small amount of Ore and doesn't use the Alchemy stuff at all. When that changes I'll likely bump up the maximums. I hope that makes sense!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/57f0c4a284a36bb146323bac45e065e20ef12204.png[/img]
The following buildings have had their resource requirements and/or pre-requisites changed (a lot of these changes are to accommodate the Storehouse limit changes). Most of the increases are in the Stone requirements as these numbers were the old numbers from when Miners got Stone rather than Workers. Workers get Stone faster than the Miners did and there is no cap on Workers. Most of the reductions are in the Wood requirements to allow you to build more stuff without needing a second Storehouse, since the Wood maximum is 40. The biggest changes are the Champion's Home (your house) and the Brewer which are WAY cheaper and easier to build now. Gotta get the Beer flowing earlier!
[list][*]Farm - reduced Wood requirement from 45 to 40
[*]Fishing Pier - reduced Wood requirement from 45 to 40. Increased maximum from 3 to 4.
[*]Champion's Home - reduced Wood and Stone requirements from 60 to 40. Also removed Stonemason prerequisite - basically you can build this much earlier than before. 
[*]Hunter Hut - reduced Wood requirement from 45 to 40, increased Stone requirement from 20 to 30. Increased maximum from 3 to 4.
[*]Tailor - reduced Wood requirement from 45 to 40, increased Stone requirement from 20 to 30.
[*]Cookhouse - reduced Wood requirement from 45 to 40, increased Stone requirement from 20 to 30. Increased maximum from 3 to 4.
[*]Herbalist - reduced Wood requirement from 45 to 40, increased Stone requirement from 20 to 40.
[*]Graveyard - reduced Stone requirement from 100 to 80
[*]Brewer - reduced Wood and Stone requirement from 100 to 40. Also changed prerequisite from an Alchemist to a Farm. This is a huge reduction allowing you to build Breweries WAY earlier than before. You can have up to four Breweries.
[*]Infirmary - reduced Wood fro 100 to 80, increased Stone from 60 to 70
[*]Tinker - increased Wood from 100 to 120.[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/62329ff130e65bce6afa8fd53cd0d5b9bdf66a5a.png[/img]
The following jobs have had their resource production updated. Most of these have been increased to take some pressure off during the early game.
[list][*]Farmers - increased the amount of Raw Veggies and Wheat that they produce per day.
[*]Brewers - now produce Beer using the production system. Also townspeople now correctly drink beer and have a mood reduction if there is no beer. This is partly why I decided to make Breweries easier to build. Can't have a bunch of angry Dwarves on day two!
[*]Cooks produce twice as many meals as they did before.
[*]Fishing Piers produce more Raw Meat - 33% increase
[*]Hunters produce more Raw Meat - more than double[/list]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/7858d9c87e19fe81cf7380c1a872a7518bc18b35.gif[/img]
Bugs stink. I blame the Goblins!
[list][*]Fixed bug that caused you to be unable to speak to a male shopkeeper if standing directly in front of him.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused townspeople to get stuck when created with their home.
[*]Cooks now correctly make food 6 times a day.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused Farmers to sometimes not drop off any raw food when harvesting.
[*]Bracers now correctly save and load
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the Male Dwarf to be offset a bit[/list]
Whew! This is a big update with a LOT of changes. Still room to tweak things if anything makes the game less fun. Balance is great, but [b]fun[/b] is more important! I need to implement the system for Tailors to make Clothing and Townspeople to need new clothes next. That's pretty much the last major resource/balance thing I want to add for now.

As always, thank you for the support and the feedback. It means a lot to me to have people who enjoy the game enough to come to the forums and tell me what they think, both the good and the critical. Thanks! :)

Oh and if you are interested in trying out the test build before it goes live, please go here for instructions for how to get it!

http://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/4/2860219962092936325/

notes.title: Test Build 1.2: Ore and Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Today's build includes the additions to the quest system that will allow you to unlock new Ore for your Miners to mine. Note existing saves should also update accordingly. So if you already have Jade armor and weapons for example, your Dwarves will be able to mine up to Jade and then you'll eventually get the quest that allows you to unlock Diamond. 

As part of this update, the maximum number of Miners has been reduced to three. I'll be working on balance more and may increase that if need be. Mostly I want to avoid the issue of getting Ore from your townspeople making things too easy. Miners can also get Coal (once you unlock it) which will be used to heat homes in an upcoming update.

In a future update I'm going to be creating some more variety in the Mine and Cave maps too.

This build also includes a number of bug fixes:
[list][*]Miners will now immediately start mining rather than trying to finish whatever goal they had when they were a worker
[*]Miners will always begin mining again after they drop off resources assuming the town storage isn't maxed out
[*]Metalworkers should no longer get stuck walking to their shop
[*]Miners will always have the correct bucket and ore when they are dropping off resources
[*]You will no longer jump on top of MushroomMen when fighting them on an incline
[*]Dwarves who get stuck while trying to chop a tree will no longer get stuck in a loop of getting stuck over and over again
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the Dwarf Choice system to swap the gender of a Dwarf, creating a Male Dwarf that has a female Dwarf texture on it.
[/list]
Also just for fun, I've been playing around with adding Apple Trees to the crops choice. Apples could be used for Food and for creating Beer (Ciders) by the Brewers.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/40177cca5e91931d9a4fb038560368187d91d360.jpg[/img]
This is NOT in the build, but figured I'd share.

I also want to extend a huge thank you to those of you who have been posting bugs and suggestions on the forums and in email for the Big Update. Your feedback is always appreciated and valuable to me and I do my best to incorporate it when I can. So...thanks! :)

If you are interested in trying out the test build go here for instructions:
http://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/4/2860219962092936325/

notes.title: Test Build 0.9: Farms and Crops
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/97a0352f0666d73b3a7d19718d706b88d46c4b0a.jpg[/img]

Test Build 0.9 includes the Farming and Crops update!

You can now speak to your farmers to change which crops they grow. At the moment, there are five options - Corn, Tomatoes, Carrots, Wheat, and Cotton.

The first three add to your town's raw food supply, which will eventually be cooked into prepared meals by the Cooks. Wheat will be used by Brewers (but can also be used to make food if the town is out of raw food) and Cotton will be used by Tailors to make Clothing. Additionally, Tailors will also be able to use Cotton to craft nice rugs for the townspeoples' homes as well as for your personal home.

Having a variety of food, both veggies and meat/fish, will increase the townspeoples' mood. I might eventually add something you have to do to get the seeds for different kinds of food but for testing purposes you can plant whatever you want right away.

Next up will be adding the resources for Hunters (raw meat and leather) and then I'll be able to attach all of the raw resources to the final products as well as build the system to allow for Cookhouse and Cooks.

If you load a previous save, the default for all of your farms will be carrots.

Things to look out for when testing are:

- Farms should immediately change their crops once you confirm the changes.
- The farm plots you set persist after saving and loading
- When the farmer drops off his crops, the correct town resources are updated. So if a farmer has carrots, corn, wheat, and cotton, you should see all four increase when s/he drops off the good at the Storehouse.

If you are interested in trying out the test build go here for instructions:
http://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/4/2860219962092936325/

notes.title: Test Build 0.8: Economy Update #1
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/d65aae26f5696cfb8efd11289f10b234d77740d6.png[/img]

Today's build includes the first phase of the Economy update, focused on adding resources gathered by townspeople and allowing you to both take from and give to the town's resources.

In this build, not all of the townspeople perform their jobs visually (meaning some don't walk to the storehouse to actually do the dropoff) but they will in a future update. Right now I wanted to get the underlying system in.

The following townspeople add resources to the town.
[list][*]Workers - quality wood or quality stone
[*]Miners - ore (all types) and coal
[*]Farmers - food, wheat, and cotton
[*]Hunters - raw meat and leather
[*]Tailors - clothing
[*]Herbalist - all alchemy resources
[*]Metalworker - handles and tools
[*]Weaponsmith - weapons
[*]Brewers - beer[/list]
The townspeople only add resources for now. In future updates I will add the system that makes them check to see if they can craft the item, such as a metalsmith needing ore to make handles or tailors needing leather or cotton to make clothing. Once that's in, they will take ingredients from the town's storage.

In addition, you will be able to tell the various townspeople who can create or gather more than one resource what to focus on, such as telling a Miner to mine Iron (assuming you have access to it) or telling a Farmer what crops to grow. This is similar to the way you can tell Workers whether to gather wood or stone. 

For now, they all just add everything (so Farmers add food, cotton, and wheat) but in the final system a single farmer will grow what you specifically tell them to. I'm letting them drop off everything for now to help test all of the resources.

Also Farmers are dropping off food. That will change once I add Cooks. Farmers will then drop off "raw vegetables" that Cooks will use to cook food, in addition to using the raw meat that hunters bring.

Lots left to do for sure, but getting the backbone of the system opens the door to add these features and more to the town economy!

If you are interested in trying out the test build go here for instructions:
http://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/4/2860219962092936325/

notes.title: Economy Update
notes.content:
Just wanted to post quick to let you all know that I'm still working on the economy update. It's been a while since the last build so I wanted to make sure I wrote something. Don't like being silent for too long!

I decided to redo the economy portion of the game to make it cleaner now that there are a LOT more resources for the town. So that's taken me a bit longer than anticipated, but I think it's worth it.

Right now I'm focusing on getting all of the new resources to add to the town correctly. With this done, the townspeople will add resources to the town based on their job. They won't need to use resources yet though and it won't be balanced.

Then I'm going to finish the system that allows you to give resources to and take resources from the town. 

After that I'll work on townspeople using resources (so a tailor will need cotton to make clothing and won't make any if there is no cotton) as well as letting you set the resource the townsperson will focus on. This means you'll be able to decide what crops to grow, which ore you want miners to mine (or coal), which Alchemy ingredients to grow, etc.

Once all of that is in and working, I'm going to do a big balance pass that will not only affect the town's resources, but also loot drops and other systems affected by resources. That will be the final phase of the economy update.

I'll try to get the first part of this in a build asap. I have the taking and giving resource system working, now I just have to hook it all up with the different resources and add more resources to the menu.

Thank you for the support and feedback everyone!

notes.title: Big Update Test Build 0.5: Resource Updates
notes.content:
[url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/396ebda58d005b48fa1cc1f5511477606da1dffd.jpg][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/396ebda58d005b48fa1cc1f5511477606da1dffd.jpg[/img][/url]

Today's test build includes a bunch of changes to the way Workers and Miners work, specifically related to gathering resources.

Workers can now either chop trees or get stone from the various rocks throughout the world. To set a Worker simply talk to her and use the "Get Stone" button to change her goal to getting Stone. You can then click the same button to set her back to "Chop Wood".

Miners now mine Copper Ore. Eventually you will be able to set them to mine any of the ores, assuming you've unlocked a mine level with access to that ore. Miners will also eventually be able to mine coal. 

Note that you cannot use the Storehouse to take ore or drop off ore yet. I'm still working on the system that will allow you to do that.

Also included is the new town menu that appears at the bottom of the screen when you are within the town's borders. I'm still tweaking it but overall I think it does a good job of giving you information without taking up too much space.

In addition to those updates, the build includes:
[list][*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the "Drop Off Resources" message in the Storehouse to remain even after you've left
[*]Fixed a bug that caused the exit in the new caves and mines to not function
[*]Updated the Cave In! quest to work correctly with the new mine layout
[*]The "Slow" trait no longer forces a townsperson to always walk. Instead, they run at a slower speed. Having them move at walk speed was just way too much of a negative
[list]

notes.title: Big Update Test Build
notes.content:
I've created a test build for anyone who would like to try out the early build of the Big Update. To get the test client, you can do the following:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - [b]HammerHelmTest[/b] - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game.

Do NOT load an old save with this build. Create a new character. 

Note the game is not balanced yet with the new systems and may not feel that different from the current Alpha just yet since the big economy changes aren't in yet. There will also likely be quite a few bugs as I'm still testing as I go. But it’ll give you a chance to check out the new characters and some of the new features as I add them and offer feedback.

What’s in this build:
[list][*]Female Characters
[*]Character creation/customization
[*]New Townspeople selection
[*]Townspeople traits (some are active, some aren’t - see below)
[*]Select Townsperson for job
[*]Getting stone from rocks (you can do this, Workers can’t yet)
[*]Crafters who have low mood or a bad crafting trait may create “shoddy” equipment
[*]Crafters with a positive crafting trait will sometimes craft a “great” item
[*]New music for title screen, overworld, and dungeons/caves.
[*]New cave maps – right now there is only one layout but I’ll be adding more variety over time,
[*]Some more optimizations for large towns
[/list]

Major stuff planned, but not in the build yet:
[list][*]Male Character and Townspeople
[*]More hair options
[*]New buildings and new townspeople jobs (hunter, tailor, and cook)
[*]Town Storage (you can drop off wood and stone tho)
[*]Most of the new town economy stuff including the new resources
[*]Miners collect ore/coal
[*]Townspeople stories and quests
[*]Town Attacks
[*]Ability to swap Townspeople jobs
[*]And more!
[/list]

These traits are working:
[list][*]Hard Worker – Chop/Mine faster
[*]Strong – Can carry more resources
[*]Weak – Carries less resources
[*]Lazy – Chops/Mines slower
[*]Fast – Runs faster
[*]Slow – Always walks
[*]Hungry – Eats more food
[*]Green Thumb – Good farmer, chops trees slower
[*]Clumsy – Sometimes makes “shoddy” items
[*]Happy – Has a permanent mood buff
[*]Claustrophobic – Slower at mining and negative mood
[*]Mole – Faster at mining and positive mood
[*]Meticulous – Sometimes crafts “Great” items, but uses more resources when crafting
[*]Drunkard – Gets a mood buff from having a drink (will eventually also get in fights)
[*]Grumpy – Permanent mood debuff (will eventually also argue with others causing mood debuffs)
[/list]

Other planned traits not active (townspeople can get these traits but they don't do anything yet):
[list][*]Brawler – Gets in fights, more likely to pick a fight if also Grumpy, good at melee
[*]Sleepy – Will sometimes go to bed, player has to wake him/her up
[*]Visual – Gets a larger mood buff from décor in the town
[*]Sickly – More likely to get sick
[*]Healthy – Less likely to get sick
[*]Pacifist – Bad at fighting, mood debuff if made Archer, Soldier, or Hunter
[*]Animal Lover – Mood debuff if Hunter
[*]Foodie – Good cook
[*]Friendly – Mood buff if any Shopkeeper
[*]Explorer – Bonus to hunting
[/list]

To get back to the Alpha client:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

notes.title: Big Update Test Build
notes.content:
I've created a test build for anyone who would like to try out the early build of the Big Update. To get the test client, you can do the following:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Enter the password to download this build - [b]HammerHelmTest[/b] - and click Check Code
5. You should get a message that the code is correct
6. Click the drop-down box and select BigUpdateTest

Steam should immediately start a new download with the test client. The new game should be called "HammerHelm [bigupdatetest]". Once the download is complete you can launch the game.

Do NOT load an old save with this build. Create a new character. 

Note the game is not balanced yet with the new systems and may not feel that different from the current Alpha just yet since the big economy changes aren't in yet. There will also likely be quite a few bugs as I'm still testing as I go. But it’ll give you a chance to check out the new characters and some of the new features as I add them and offer feedback.

What’s in this build:
[list][*]Female Characters
[*]Character creation/customization
[*]New Townspeople selection
[*]Townspeople traits (some are active, some aren’t - see below)
[*]Select Townsperson for job
[*]Getting stone from rocks (you can do this, Workers can’t yet)
[*]Crafters who have low mood or a bad crafting trait may create “shoddy” equipment
[*]Crafters with a positive crafting trait will sometimes craft a “great” item
[*]New music for title screen, overworld, and dungeons/caves.
[*]New cave maps – right now there is only one layout but I’ll be adding more variety over time,
[*]Some more optimizations for large towns
[/list]

Major stuff planned, but not in the build yet:
[list][*]Male Character and Townspeople
[*]More hair options
[*]New buildings and new townspeople jobs (hunter, tailor, and cook)
[*]Town Storage (you can drop off wood and stone tho)
[*]Most of the new town economy stuff including the new resources
[*]Miners collect ore/coal
[*]Townspeople stories and quests
[*]Town Attacks
[*]Ability to swap Townspeople jobs
[*]And more!
[/list]

These traits are working:
[list][*]Hard Worker – Chop/Mine faster
[*]Strong – Can carry more resources
[*]Weak – Carries less resources
[*]Lazy – Chops/Mines slower
[*]Fast – Runs faster
[*]Slow – Always walks
[*]Hungry – Eats more food
[*]Green Thumb – Good farmer, chops trees slower
[*]Clumsy – Sometimes makes “shoddy” items
[*]Happy – Has a permanent mood buff
[*]Claustrophobic – Slower at mining and negative mood
[*]Mole – Faster at mining and positive mood
[*]Meticulous – Sometimes crafts “Great” items, but uses more resources when crafting
[*]Drunkard – Gets a mood buff from having a drink (will eventually also get in fights)
[*]Grumpy – Permanent mood debuff (will eventually also argue with others causing mood debuffs)
[/list]

Other planned traits not active (townspeople can get these traits but they don't do anything yet):
[list][*]Brawler – Gets in fights, more likely to pick a fight if also Grumpy, good at melee
[*]Sleepy – Will sometimes go to bed, player has to wake him/her up
[*]Visual – Gets a larger mood buff from décor in the town
[*]Sickly – More likely to get sick
[*]Healthy – Less likely to get sick
[*]Pacifist – Bad at fighting, mood debuff if made Archer, Soldier, or Hunter
[*]Animal Lover – Mood debuff if Hunter
[*]Foodie – Good cook
[*]Friendly – Mood buff if any Shopkeeper
[*]Explorer – Bonus to hunting
[/list]

To get back to the Alpha client:

1. In the Steam Client Library where it lists all of your games, right click on HammerHelm
2. Click Preferences
3. In the window that opens, select the "Betas" Tab
4. Choose “None” from the drop down
5. Steam should then revert back to the Alpha client

To get the latest updates on the Big Update and to post feedback or bugs, please visit the Big Update forum.

http://steamcommunity.com/app/664000/discussions/4/

notes.title: Big Update Progress
notes.content:
I'm working on the Big Update that I've mentioned a few times and I wanted to show you all some progress.

The new female Dwarves are in the game and there is a new system for choosing Dwarves to join your town and choosing which Dwarf gets assigned which jobs.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VNv3FFhG6z8&feature=youtu.be
Each Dwarf will have traits that determine how good s/he is at certain jobs and activities. Lazy Dwarves work slow, strong Dwarves can carry more resources, meticulous Dwarves will craft better items, and sleepy Dwarves might take a nap while on the job!

Every time you place a home, you'll be presented with three Dwarves and you can choose two of them to join your town. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/2d46ccabec6f5e042645ef0b74e03c73e2578d56.gif[/img]

These features are just a small part of the Big Update, which will include more buildings, more jobs, a totally redesigned town economy (including allowing you to get resources like gold and ore from the town) and a ton more. I'm hoping to write a comprehensive announcement about the Big Update soon. My plan is for the Big Update to bring HammerHelm out of Alpha and into Beta.

Thank you again everyone for supporting HammerHelm!

Oh and the new male Dwarf is almost done too! [i](don't worry, he will have eyes - and of course, different beards to choose from! :P)[/i]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9aebcc2f1cf97220923620ef3df9a418529f124c.gif[/img]

notes.title: Alpha Build 0.8.8: Loot Update and Changes to Dash Attack
notes.content:
Today's build includes a change to the loot system to help spread out the kind of loot you get. Normally when you get alchemy or ore as loot, you get one big stack of the same type. This new system will sometimes give you smaller stacks of different types. So for example, rather than just getting a stack of 6 Jade Ore, you might get 3 Iron and 3 Jade or get 2 Jade and 4 Gold. 

Build 0.8.8 also includes:
[list][*]Dash attack now uses 60 stamina
[list][*]Dash is meant to be a "first strike" attack rather than something that is used over and over again in the same combat[/list]
[*]Dash attack will no longer work if you are facing a monster that is already in melee range
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused Diamond Ore Deposits to give Gold Ore
[*]Fixed a typo related to the Mage Tower teleporter

notes.title: Alpha Build 0.8.7: Potion Buff and Optimizations
notes.content:
Alpha 0.8.7 includes a big buff to healing potions that increases the amount of hit points restored from all levels of heal potions. The heal potions in your inventory and hotbar will update automatically, however any heal potions in storage will not. To update those, drag them into your inventory and then save and reload the game.

This build also includes:
[list][*]Optimized the water to increase overall framerate a bit
[*]Reduced the chance of a monster spawner creating 4 monsters at higher levels
[*]Updated all shields mouse-over text to reflect that they do not stun or knockdown enemies anymore[/list]
I hope everyone has a safe and happy New Year!!!

notes.title: Development Roadmap Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/37c481b8154ff95f19f84a4decd6407edb4dd608.png[/img]
A quick update about some new stuff I am working on, short-term and long-term for HammerHelm. And by "quick", I mean lots and lots of stuff. :)

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/d258a839d84a3a8d301d128b473562e9d7475322.png[/img]
I've been wanting to do this for a while now. Aside from uploading builds, HammerHelm isn't really integrated with Steam much. Achievements is a good starting point for that. I have about 10 planned to start and will add more over time once the core system is hooked up.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9c0d8f3eae0e9ae51640ee0f898ab09994fa7474.png[/img]
This will be a bit of work as the save system is some of the oldest code in the game and it can't be used as an auto-save. When you save the game in the ESC menu you'll notice a few second delay. That's fine when you're leaving the game, but would be awful for an auto-save. Still, it's an important improvement so worth refactoring.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/bb3c48bfb71457c6d4532d07f924f041bed16d32.png[/img]
With very large towns, sometimes framerate can drop more than I'd like. Thankfully there is quite a bit of room for optimization with the buildings, NPCs, and the surrounding wilderness.


[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/d7a7b42d2d8a1cb4d2f694d883f8199ae51a2f16.png[/img]
That's some of the shorter-term stuff. Longer term I'm in the process of designing a big update to the game. This is still in the design phase, but I'm really happy with it and I'm about ready to start working on it, so I figured I'd share.

Part of the reason I am working on things like Achievements or Key Binding is because of the stuff I outline below. It's all interconnected (which will make the game even better!) and while I am finishing designing it, I want to avoid working on stuff that might wind up needing to be changed to fit the new and updated features. 

I'm working in parallel essentially, updating the current game to add some of the missing core features that most games have, while working behind the scenes on what will be a big update, [b]and hopefully huge improvement[/b], to the game. The core game will still be about building your town and adventuring, but I think these updates, along with some other stuff, will make for a better game with more things to experience. Note this isn't the full list, but these three features are the core of what I want to update.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/daaa75d907b7a0441f1167a5776964520167171d.png[/img]
Add more resources and more ways to get them. 
[list][*]Questing feels grindy because it's the only way to get resources you need for yourself.
[*]If you need leather, but the game keeps giving you quests to fight monsters that drop ore and alchemy ingredients, it can be frustrating. 
[*]Even if I updated the system to know what you need and increase the chance of getting it, it still makes quests seem more grindy because you're always waiting for the next one.
[*]I want to add more resources and more ways to get those resources from the town rather than quests.
[*]This will make quests more like special events, rather than a necessary resource gathering mechanism
[*]This also means that I'll be adding more things for you to do aside from questing, so you're never idle waiting for a quest. There's always something else do to and you aren't blocked just because the right quest didn't appear![/list]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/9bc9a1d1e336f67ec1efc382dc425f3c84d79462.png[/img]
Add meaningful personality to the townspeople. 
[list][*]I want the Dwarves in your town to feel special, rather than just crafting stations and quest givers, by giving them more personality and stories.
[*]The idea here is to start with why the Dwarf left and joined your clan. It could be anything from he's in debt (opening the possibility of the people he owes money to coming after him!) or s/he just wanted a new adventure. 
[*]Traits and histories would offer bonuses and penalties, such as the Dwarf in debt charges more for crafting (if you make him a crafter) or a lazy Dwarf who always walk slow.
[*]There will be quests and events tied to the Dwarves based on their backstories and traits, adding even more to their stories.
[*]All of this means of course that you’ll be able to choose which Dwarf gets a job and be able to switch them around[/list]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/eb48e415b4bce3b6daae23334e58ed15dac56485.png[/img]
Add a more meaningful economy. This ties a bit to resources, but is more focused on creating opportunities for choices.
[list][*]There are very few resources and they don't play off of each other. 
[*]You don't really have to choose to spend resources on something for yourself or something for the town.
[*]Right now the town's resources (wood, stone, etc.) and separate from what you need to craft (ore, leather, etc.) - I want to combine them so you're making choices for yourself vs. stuff for the town.
[*]Because the resources are more shared, you'll be able to gather more kinds of resources for the town in addition to for yourself.
[*]This also means that the townspeople would be gathering resources that are useful to the town AND you, such as ore and gold.
[*]With the town, I want to add more dials and switches to play with so to speak and give you more things to do aside from just questing..[/list]
There's more planned but I wanted to give you an idea about some of the bigger stuff in the works. The goal is to make a more varied and personal experience while maintaining what you all like about the game now.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/96cf35fd89706630c93f88e68b2abdfe421e9fb1.png[/img]
In addition to all of that, the new female Dwarf model is well underway. I'll have an update on the characters in a couple of weeks. I'm really looking forward to replacing some of the placeholder art, especially the Dwarves. For those of you that missed it, here's the concept art for the female Dwarf.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/de76a2c29f77a06b2e7f51ac40ee9c3f05f307ec.png[/img]

I'm also looking to update the look of the caves, add a new day/night cycle (and maybe weather and seasons), add more options for farms (such as crop types), new buildings and townspeople jobs, and more interdependency between the various town buildings. Oh and if I can find the time, I want to do a small holiday update as well with more limited edition items.

So... lots going on. I also wanted to say thank you for coming along on this journey with me! I very much appreciate the support and feedback.

[*]With the town, I want to add more dials and switches to play with so to speak and give you more things to do aside from just questing..[/list]
There's more planned but I wanted to give you an idea about some of the bigger stuff in the works. The goal is to make a more varied and personal experience while maintaining what you all like about the game now.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/96cf35fd89706630c93f88e68b2abdfe421e9fb1.png[/img]
In addition to all of that, the new female Dwarf model is well underway. I'll have an update on the characters in a couple of weeks. I'm really looking forward to replacing some of the placeholder art, especially the Dwarves. For those of you that missed it, here's the concept art for the female Dwarf.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/de76a2c29f77a06b2e7f51ac40ee9c3f05f307ec.png[/img]

I'm also looking to update the look of the caves, add a new day/night cycle (and maybe weather and seasons), add more options for farms (such as crop types), new buildings and townspeople jobs, and more interdependency between the various town buildings. Oh and if I can find the time, I want to do a small holiday update as well with more limited edition items.

So... lots going on. I also wanted to say thank you for coming along on this journey with me! I very much appreciate the support and feedback.

notes.title: Female Dwarves + Early Access Exclusives!
notes.content:
I wanted to share this with everyone as I am really excited to be making some great progress towards changing out the Dwarf character model and adding female Dwarves!

[h1] [b] [i]*** Note that some of the hair styles will be exclusive to Early Access players! ***[/i] [/b] [/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29603119/de76a2c29f77a06b2e7f51ac40ee9c3f05f307ec.png[/img]

I'm really thrilled with how she looks. The concept artist I am working with did an amazing job. I can already picture her wearing some armored shoulder pads and wielding a hammer and shield!

The bracers will be separate and those will become craftables just like the armor shoulder pads. Once I have those in I'm going to replace the current belt and fauld with left and right bracers since those two items don't really fit anymore. They'll also have metal trim for each of the crafting metal types.

For the first round, we're building hair styles A, C, and H. Since I'm working with a new 3D artist for the first time I want to make sure everything works properly before creating a bunch more hair styles. I also wanted to start with longer styles since those are the trickiest to get to look good. I want the hair to sway a bit as she runs and fights. After that I'll likely have the rest built.

You'll be able to pick her hair style and color and hopefully her tunic color as well. I have to build all of that since the current character doesn't support any kind of real customization.

The 3D model for the character and the hair styles are already in progress. She's higher quality than the current model and should look a lot better overall.

The new male Dwarf's concept sketches have just started and I'll show him as soon as I can!

notes.title: Alpha 0.6.0: New Combat System!
notes.content:
The new combat system is live as part of the Alpha 6 release! 

The new "How To Fight" UI can be accessed from the Title Screen or in game through the ESC menu if you need a refresher.

At first the system may seem a bit complex, but really all you need to remember to fight effectively is:

- Left click to attack
- Right click to block
- Middle button or R to use power attack

For those of you who have been playing HammerHelm for a while, the new system may take a bit of getting used to. I think it's way more fun though and I hope you do too!

As part of this update monster damage has been reduced as well. I will be tweaking that along with health potion heal amounts as I get more feedback on the new system.

Thank you again everyone for giving feedback during the combat system's development!

https://youtu.be/Uetzcr1ml4Q
In the video you'll see the new system, including the faster basic attacks and the power attack. Scoring three hits in a row without getting hit yourself unlocks a power attack. You'll know when it's unlocked by both the sword icon near your health bar filling up and turning green and a lightning ball effect that appears on your hand. Pressing middle mouse button or the "R" key will initiate the attack. 

In the first fight I manage to kill both Goblins without taking a hit. In the second, I get a little too aggressive and get hit twice while trying to get one more attack in before the monster's attack. You'll note that just because you unlock a power attack doesn't mean you HAVE to use it right away. If a monster is about to attack, you can block it's attack, and then counter with the power attack. So timing matters a lot more than it did in the previous system.

The basic attacks do less damage than the current attacks, but the power attack deals MUCH more damage. Combined with the character attacking faster, performing power attacks allows you to kill monsters faster than the current system.

In the future I plan on adding different power attacks based on what kind of weapon you are wielding.

notes.title: New Combat System Update 2
notes.content:
https://youtu.be/Uetzcr1ml4Q
The system is now fully hooked into the actual game. I'm still testing parts of it though so I'd like to wait until Thursday (Sept 21) to release it. Chopping trees and mining ore works as well. I need to test the system with all of the monsters and I want to tweak some aspects of the system regarding how monsters move around during a fight.

In the video you'll see the new system, including the faster basic attacks and the power attack. Scoring three hits in a row without getting hit yourself unlocks a power attack. You'll know when it's unlocked by both the sword icon near your health bar filling up and turning green and a lightning ball effect that appears on your hand. Pressing middle mouse button or the "R" key will initiate the attack. 

The basic attacks do less damage than the current attacks, but the power attack deals MUCH more damage. Combined with the character attacking faster, performing power attacks allows you to kill monsters faster than the current system.

In the first fight I manage to kill both Goblins without taking a hit. In the second, I get a little too aggressive and get hit twice while trying to get one more attack in before the monster's attack. You'll note that just because you unlock a power attack doesn't mean you HAVE to use it right away. If a monster is about to attack, you can block it's attack, and then counter with the power attack. So timing matters a lot more than it did in the previous system.

Overall the system is more forgiving than the current system and far more reliable as far as hitting when you feel like your attack should have hit. Blocking is now also a legitimate tactic as blocking doesn't interrupt your power gain. You can also turn your character while blocking. Holding a block doesn't currently use stamina yet, but it will. That's the last part of the new system that I have to add.

Note, you can theoretically back away from the monsters to avoid damage as well, similar to the current system. Doing so risks losing any power that you have gained. So it's far less efficient and will prolong fights. 

After the system is live I will likely continue to tweak it. I also want to create different power attacks for each weapon type. So the sword might do extra damage to one monster while a hammer might damage multiple monsters but not for quite as much as the sword.

notes.content:
https://youtu.be/Uetzcr1ml4Q
The system is now fully hooked into the actual game. I'm still testing parts of it though so I'd like to wait until Thursday (Sept 21) to release it. Chopping trees and mining ore works as well. I need to test the system with all of the monsters and I want to tweak some aspects of the system regarding how monsters move around during a fight.

In the video you'll see the new system, including the faster basic attacks and the power attack. Scoring three hits in a row without getting hit yourself unlocks a power attack. You'll know when it's unlocked by both the sword icon near your health bar filling up and turning green and a lightning ball effect that appears on your hand. Pressing middle mouse button or the "R" key will initiate the attack. 

The basic attacks do less damage than the current attacks, but the power attack deals MUCH more damage. Combined with the character attacking faster, performing power attacks allows you to kill monsters faster than the current system.

In the first fight I manage to kill both Goblins without taking a hit. In the second, I get a little too aggressive and get hit twice while trying to get one more attack in before the monster's attack. You'll note that just because you unlock a power attack doesn't mean you HAVE to use it right away. If a monster is about to attack, you can block it's attack, and then counter with the power attack. So timing matters a lot more than it did in the previous system.

Overall the system is more forgiving than the current system and far more reliable as far as hitting when you feel like your attack should have hit. Blocking is now also a legitimate tactic as blocking doesn't interrupt your power gain. You can also turn your character while blocking. Holding a block doesn't currently use stamina yet, but it will. That's the last part of the new system that I have to add.

Note, you can theoretically back away from the monsters to avoid damage as well, similar to the current system. Doing so risks losing any power that you have gained. So it's far less efficient and will prolong fights. 

After the system is live I will likely continue to tweak it. I also want to create different power attacks for each weapon type. So the sword might do extra damage to one monster while a hammer might damage multiple monsters but not for quite as much as the sword.

notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
I'm working on a number of things and I wanted to give everyone an update! First a sneak peak at a new structure in development, the Fishing Pier:

[img]http://www.hammerhelm.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/Fishing-Pier-WIP-1.png[/img]

The Fishing Pier will work similar to a farm as it will generate food as well. Having diverse food will provide a mood buff. In addition, a quest that adversely affects your farms won't necessarily affect the fishing pier, reducing the impact that a single quest will have on your food production. Another planned building is the Woodchopper. They will cut down trees (to avoid using your stored wood) to create firewood and increases the speed at which all cut down trees regrow. Reducing the regrowth time will reduce the time it takes Workers to collect Quality Wood since they wont have to walk as far to find a fully grown tree. 

Some other things I am working on:

[b]More Optimization[/b]
Overall the new world map is pretty well optimized, so now I want to tackle the town itself. There are a lot of buildings that could use an optimization pass to help improve framerate when in large towns. This work is a bit tedious (ok, it's really, really boring!) but it'll help. I already have the Wooden House optimized and will be working on more buildings over time.

[b]Combat[/b]
I just started working on a new combat system that will hopefully be more dynamic and more fun. In the new system, an attack steps the character forward and knocks the monster backwards. It feels a lot more fun in my opinion. I'm planning on releasing a test map with the very early version of the new combat system on it so you all can check it out. There will be other improvements to the way monsters attack and defensive maneuvers (like blocking and dodging) as well.

[b]More Quests[/b]
I have a bunch of quests that I want to add to the game, including a few related to Shaydee the Goblin, existing late stage buildings such as the Weaponsmith, Armorsmith, Brewery and the Tavern, and the new structures. I'll be adding these over time while working on larger updates.

[b]Champion's House Updates[/b]
I want to add storage chests and the ability to display items in your house. With the ability to sell items to Shaydee in place storage isn't as important as it was before, but it's still something I want to add.

[b]Town Updates[/b]
I want to add more uses for the structures you can place in your town. This includes but is not limited to, making wells provide fresh water to nearby homes and mood buffs for placing decor such as fountains, town trees, and lamp-posts, etc. I'm also going to add a road placer soon as I know that is a very popular request. I'm also working on a system for the Tavernkeeper called "Rumors" which will allow you to get quests that you want. For example, let's say you need more ore to make your weapons. The best place to get ore is Caves of course. So you could ask the tavernkeeper to keep his ears open for anyone who has found a cave, greatly increasing your chances to get a Cave related quest. There also could be rumors that create brand new quests as well.

[b]Steam Achievements[/b]
Not a huge priority at the moment unless you all really want them. Open to feedback on this with regards to priority.

[b]World Map POIs Update[/b]
This includes adding more gameplay for the current POIs on the map, including the big fort to the north. There's also room on the map for at least two more interesting POI so I'll be adding those after the current areas are fleshed out more.

There's more in development than what is above, but I wanted to give you all a high level overview of the current updates that I have planned in the near future. As development continues and I get more feedback these priorities could shift so I'll likely be writing these kinds of Dev Updates every so often to keep you all up to date.

As always, thank you very much for supporting HammerHelm and for your great feedback! Very much appreciated.

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna
